# Gradle Grammar-Kit Plugin

<tldr>
Current Release: 2023.3.0.3

GitHub: [Releases &amp; Changelog](https://github.com/JetBrains/gradle-grammar-kit-plugin/releases), [Issue Tracker](https://github.com/JetBrains/gradle-grammar-kit-plugin/issues)
</tldr>

The [Gradle Grammar-Kit Plugin](https://github.com/JetBrains/gradle-grammar-kit-plugin) automates generating lexers and parsers to support building [custom language](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/custom-language-support.html) plugins for IntelliJ-based IDEs when using [Grammar-Kit](https://github.com/JetBrains/Grammar-Kit).

Note: Known Limitations

The plugin does not support two-pass generation. Therefore, it does not support method mixins.

Tip:

Please see [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/JetBrains/gradle-grammar-kit-plugin/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) on how to submit feedback and contribute to this project.

Before visiting the [Issue Tracker](https://github.com/JetBrains/gradle-grammar-kit-plugin/issues), update both plugin and Gradle to the latest versions.

## Usage

To enable this plugin in your Gradle-based project, register the plugin in the Gradle build script's `plugins` section:

Kotlin:

```KOTLIN
plugins {
  id("org.jetbrains.grammarkit") version "2023.3.0.3"
}
```

Groovy:

```GROOVY
plugins {
  id "org.jetbrains.grammarkit" version "2023.3.0.3"
}
```

Tip: Minimum Gradle Version

This project requires Gradle 7.4 or newer.
However, it is recommended to use the latest Gradle available.
See [Gradle Installation](https://gradle.org/install/) guide.

## Configuration

See also [Usage Examples](#usage-examples) below.

### Grammar-Kit Extension

After the Gradle Grammar-Kit Plugin is applied, the `grammarKit` extension can be used to configure the plugin and common settings of the provided tasks.

Tip:

In most cases, explicit configuration can be omitted.

Example:

Kotlin:

```KOTLIN
grammarKit {
  jflexRelease.set("1.7.0-1")
  grammarKitRelease.set("2021.1.2")
}
```

Groovy:

```GROOVY
grammarKit {
  jflexRelease = "1.7.0-1"
  grammarKitRelease = "2021.1.2"
}
```

#### grammarKitRelease

The release version of the [Grammar-Kit](https://github.com/JetBrains/Grammar-Kit) to use.

Type
: `String`

Default value
: `2022.3.2`

#### jflexRelease

The version of the IntelliJ-patched JFlex, a [fork of JFlex](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-deps-jflex) lexer generator for IntelliJ Platform API.

Type
: `String`

Default value
: `1.9.2`

#### intellijRelease

An optional IntelliJ IDEA version to build the classpath for [GenerateParser](#generateparser-task) and [GenerateLexer](#generatelexer-task) tasks.

If provided, [grammarKitRelease](#grammar-kit-extension-grammarkitrelease) and [jflexRelease](#grammar-kit-extension-jflexrelease) properties are ignored as both dependencies will be provided from the given IntelliJ IDEA release.

Type
: `String`

Default value
: `null`

## Tasks

### generateLexer

The `generateLexer` task generates a lexer for the given grammar.

The following sections describe task configuration options.
See also [Grammar-Kit Extension](#grammar-kit-extension) for common configuration.

#### sourceFile

The source `.*flex` file to generate the lexer from.

Required
: yes

Type
: `String`

#### targetOutputDir

The path to the target directory for the generated lexer.

Required
: yes

Type
: `String`

#### skeleton

An optional path to the skeleton file to use for the generated lexer.
The path will be provided as the `--skel` option.
By default, it uses the `[idea-flex.skeleton](https://raw.github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/master/tools/lexer/idea-flex.skeleton)` skeleton file.

Type
: `String`

Default
: `null`

#### purgeOldFiles

Purge old files from the target directory before generating the lexer.

Type
: `Boolean`

Default
: `false`

### generateParser

The `generateParser` task generates a parser for the given grammar.

The following sections describe task configuration options.
See also [Grammar-Kit Extension](#grammar-kit-extension) for common configuration.

#### sourceFile

The source `.bnf` file to generate the parser from.

Required
: yes

Type
: `String`

#### targetRootOutputDir

The path to the target directory for the generated parser.

Type
: `String`

Default
: `null`

#### pathToParser

The location of the generated parser class, relative to the [targetRootOutputDir](#tasks-generateparser-targetrootOutputDir).

Required
: yes

Type
: `String`

#### pathToPsiRoot

The location of the generated PSI files, relative to the [targetRootOutputDir](#tasks-generateparser-targetrootOutputDir).

Required
: yes

Type
: `String`

#### purgeOldFiles

Purge old files from the target directory before generating the parser.

Type
: `Boolean`

Default
: `false`

# Internal Actions Menu

The `Tools | Internal Actions` menu provides plugin developers with a suite of tools to help develop, debug, and test their IntelliJ Platform plugins.

Tip:

If the menu item `Tools | Internal Actions` is not available in the IDE, then the first step is [Enabling Internal Mode](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/enabling-internal.html).

Click on the following topics to learn more about the `Internal Actions` menu.

* [Enabling Internal Mode](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/enabling-internal.html) provides instructions for enabling the Internal Actions menu.

* [UI Tools](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/internal-ui-sub.html) has information about some tools for inspecting and testing plugin UI.



# Enabling Internal Mode

There are useful tools, such as the Internal Actions menu, that are only visible if the internal mode is enabled in the IDE.

Procedure: Configuring Internal Mode



# Internal Actions - UI Submenu

The Internal Actions UI submenu provides IntelliJ Platform plugin developers with a suite of tools to help develop, debug, and test their IntelliJ Platform project UI.

Tip:

If the menu item `Tools | Internal Actions` is not available in the IDE, then the first step is [Enabling Internal Mode](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/enabling-internal.html).

## The Tools Available on the UI Submenu

Here are some tools available on the UI submenu of the Internal Actions menu:

* [UI Inspector](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/internal-ui-inspector.html) is a tool to get an internal description with each UI element's properties.

* [LaF Defaults](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/internal-ui-laf-defaults.html) provides a way to lookup the key-value pair for a UI element, and the ability to prototype the color of UI Controls.



# Internal Actions – UI Inspector

The UI Inspector is a tool to interrogate elements of the IDE's UI to get an internal description of each element.

Tip:

If the menu item `Tools | Internal Actions` is not available in the IDE, then the first step is [Enabling Internal Mode](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/enabling-internal.html).

## Using the UI Inspector

Centering the cursor on a UI element and pressing `Ctrl+Alt` (`Ctrl+Option` on macOS) when clicking the left mouse button reveals the properties of the Swing component.

For example, to get information about the Build Project button's "hammer" icon on the toolbar (highlighted in green), put the mouse cursor on the icon and press `Ctrl/Cmd+Alt` while clicking the mouse.

The UI Inspector displays the icon details:

![Internal Icon Info](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/internal_ui_inspector_icon_info.png)

## 

`added-at` Property

Sometimes, inspecting a complex component's properties is not enough to understand how the component was created and configured.
UI Inspector gives the possibility of finding the code where the selected component was added, which makes it much easier to understand which APIs can be used to build custom components with similar complexity.

To find the place where the component was added, select the added-at property to show the stack trace:

![added-at stack trace](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/internal_ui_inspector_added_at.png)

## Accessibility Checks

Since 2025.2, the UI Inspector includes the Show Accessibility Issues button that enables inspections for common accessibility problems, similar to browser tools like Google Chrome Lighthouse or apps like Accessibility Insights for Windows.
These issues are usually invisible in the UI, but they can still prevent users who rely on assistive technologies like screen readers or voice control from interacting with the UI.

For each problem, the affected value in the Properties table contains a description that explains what it affects and how to fix it.

![Accessibility Checks](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/internal_ui_inspector_accessibility_checks.png)
Tip:

Refer to the [accessibility guidelines](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/accessibility.html) to learn more about accessibility best practices.



# Internal Actions - LaF Defaults

The LaF Defaults window provides a key-value pair lookup for UI Controls.
It also allows interactive prototyping of UI Control color changes.

LaF stands for Look and Feel, see [Swing Tutorial](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/uiswing/lookandfeel/index.html) for more details.

Tip:

If the menu item `Tools | Internal Actions` is not available in the IDE, then the first step is [Enabling Internal Mode](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/enabling-internal.html).

## Opening LaF Defaults

The LaF Defaults window is opened by selecting the menu item `Tools | Internal Actions | UI | LaF Defaults`.

It has two columns representing key-value pairs for UI Controls:

* The Name column contains the UI Control `key` for each IntelliJ Platform UI element available at runtime.

* The Value column contains the UI Control color `value` for each IntelliJ Platform UI element.

## Using the LaF Panel

### Finding UI Controls

The LaF Defaults window is used interactively by entering a UI element type - e.g. `Panel` - in the Filter text box at the top.
LaF Defaults shows the list of UI Control names matching the filter.

Enable Colors only to show only entries with color value.

Clicking on one of the names narrows the information to show only the key-value pair for that UI element:

![LaF Lookup](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/internal_lafd_win.png)

### Prototyping the Color of UI Controls

The color of UI Controls can be changed (in real time) by clicking in the Value column next to a Name (`key`) of interest.
The Choose Color window is displayed.
Color changes can be specified as RGB, HSB, hexadecimal, or using the graphical color picker.
Pressing the Choose button changes the UI Control color immediately.

UI Control colors can be reset using the Choose Color window, or by resetting the [theme](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/settings-appearance.html).

* [Stripes](#stripes) on the left and right sides that provide quick access to tool windows

IntelliJ Platform also provides the following container elements:

* [Dialogs](#dialogs)

* [Popups](#popups)

* [Notifications](#notifications)

See the full list of UI components in [Components](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/components.html).

which means that the user may hide unnecessary widgets and buttons and add new ones.

The IntelliJ code editor provides highlighting, navigation, refactorings, and other powerful code insights features.
See implementation details in [Editor basics](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/editor-basics.html).

### Editor tabs

Tabs display the file name and extension. They can be [pinned](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/using-code-editor.html#pin-or-unpin-a-tab), [opened in separate windows](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/using-code-editor.html#detach_tab) or in a [split view](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/using-code-editor.html#split_screen).

![Editor tabs](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/ui_overview_tabs.png)
See more details on working with tabs in the editor in [Editor tabs](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/using-code-editor.html#manage_tabs). For UI component reference, go to [Tabs](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/tabs.html).

### Inspection widget

A small control in the top-right corner of the editor shows the number of errors, warnings, and typos and allows navigating to the detailed view in the Project tool window.

![Inspection widget](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/ui_overview_inspection_widget.png)
See more in [File and project analysis](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/file-and-project-analysis.html#analysis-current-file).

### Gutter

A vertical area along the left side of the editor that provides important information and action icons within easy reach. It shows line numbers and buttons for folding, navigating, and running and debugging code along with VCS stripes and other controls.

![Editor gutter](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/ui_overview_gutter.png)
See more in [Editor gutter](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/editor-gutter.html).

### Inlays

Hints that show additional information like parameter types or variable values and interactive controls for showing annotations, usages, and more.

![Inlays](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/ui_overview_inlays.png)
See more in [implementation details](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/inlay-hints.html) and [user guidelines](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/inlay-hints.html).

### Floating toolbar

A small toolbar that appears when you select a code fragment in the editor. It contains buttons and controls for the most popular actions relevant in the current context,
such as quick fixes, AI-actions, basic refactorings, and code-formatting options:

![Floating toolbar](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/ui_overview_floating_toolbar.png)
See more in [Floating toolbar](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/working-with-source-code.html#floating_toolbar).

## Status bar

The status bar on the bottom of the main window displays information on the current state of the project and the IDE as well as the path to the currently opened file:

![Status bar](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/ui_overview_status_bar.png)
### Navigation bar

The left part of the status bar by default is occupied by the navigation bar that is a compact alternative for the Project tool window.
It shows a path to the selected file and allows you to go to other files and directories using this path:

![Navigation bar](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/ui_overview_navigation_bar.png)

### Status bar widgets

The right part of the status bar contains status bar widgets which show statuses of various IDE and project settings and provide actions for changing these settings.
For example, the indent widget shows the number of spaces for code formatting in the current file and allows users to change this number:

![Status bar widget](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/ui_overview_status_bar_widget.png)
See more information on status bar widgets implementation in [Status Bar Widgets](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/status-bar-widgets.html).

## Dialogs

In the IntelliJ Platform, dialogs are modal windows that appear over the main application screen and require user actions to proceed.
The dialogs might be used for different purposes, such as setting up the IDE and projects, creating new instances, asking for confirmations, and so on.

### Dialog examples

Settings:

![Settings dialog](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/ui_overview_settings.png)
Welcome screen:

![Welcome screen](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/ui_overview_welcome_screen.png)
New project wizard:

![New project wizard](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/ui_overview_new_project.png)

## Popups

A popup is a lightweight window that appears above the application screen. Unlike the dialogs, popups do not have the standard OS
title bar and are usually dismissed by clicking outside.

### Popup examples

Completion popup:

![Completion popup](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/ui_overview_completion.png)
Documentation popup:

![Documentation popup](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/ui_overview_documentation.png)

## Notifications

In IntelliJ Platform, different components are used to inform users about various events and status changes, depending on the severity and context of the message.

### Balloons

[Notification balloons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/balloon.html) inform users on the events or system states related to a project or IDE:

![Notification balloon](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/ui_overview_balloon.png)

### Alerts

Alerts are modal windows that draw the user's attention to crucial information or ask for confirmation before proceeding:

![Alert](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/ui_overview_alert.png)

### Banners

[Banners](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/banner.html) appear on top of the editor or in tool windows. They inform the user about the state of a specific context and suggest context-related actions and quick fixes.

![Banner](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/ui_overview_banner.png)

## Context menus

Context menus list actions available in the current context and open on right-click:

![Context menu](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/ui_overview_menu.png)

# Button

<tldr>
Implementation:
[JButton](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/uiswing/components/button.html)
</tldr>

![Cancel and Save buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_example.png)

## When to use

Use a button to invoke an immediate action:

![When to use a button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_when_to_use.png)

## When not to use

| ![Using links instead of buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_link_instead.png) |Use a link instead if:                         * The action takes the user to another page of the same dialog or an external source like documentation. Note: Exception: the Next and Previous buttons in wizard navigation.    * The command is a secondary action that isn't related to the primary purpose of the window, and the space is constrained.                    |
| ![Using toolbar buttons instead of buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_toolbar.png) |Use a [toolbar button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/toolbar.html) instead if there are several buttons related to a table or list.                    |
| ![Using split buttons instead of buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_split_button.png) |Use a [split button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/split-button.html) instead if:                         * There are more than two related actions, but the space is limited and/or packed.    * The action isn't common and is dangerous, for example, can destroy user data and cannot be easily undone.                    |
|                      ![Using built-in buttons instead of buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_built_in_button.png)                  |Use a [built-in button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/built-in-button.html) instead if it's related to an input field, combo box,                     search field.                    |

## How to use

### Label

Use an action name as a button label.

#### Use title capitalization

Use [title capitalization](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/capitalization.html) for button labels.

#### Use imperative verbs

Write the label as an imperative verb, for example, Save, Print, Cancel. Use title capitalization.

Note:
Exceptions: standard buttons like OK, Back/Forward,
Previous/Next, Yes/No, Agree,
Options, Settings, Details.

#### Be specific

The button should answer the question in the title, so the user can skip the description. Prefer specific
labels over
generic ones:

Correct
![Specific button in a dialog](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_delete_dialog.png)
Incorrect
![Generic button in a dialog](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_delete_dialog_incorrect.png)
Note:

Exception: the Cancel button if it's clear what action is being canceled.
For example, use
Cancel instead of Don’t Delete.

Do not
use the word
Now in labels because buttons always trigger an immediate action:

|                              Correct                             ![A button with 'Check for Updates' label](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_check_for_updates.png)                          |Incorrect                             ![A button with 'Check Now' label](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_check_now.png) |

#### Be short and clear

The label should be short, not more than five words. If it’s not obvious what element the button is related
to, add more
words to make it clear. Prefer clear labels to short ones:

| Correct                             ![A button with the 'Edit Action Icon...' label](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_active_edit_action.png) |Acceptable                             ![A button with 'Edit' label](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_edit.png) |

#### Ellipsis

* Add an ellipsis if additional actions such as adding more info or confirming the action are required.

* Don't add an ellipsis if another window is opened, but no more input from the user is required. For example, About, Details.

![Buttons with ellipsis](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_ellipsis.png)

### Button states

#### Default

![Default button on macOS and Windows](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_default.png)
* The default button confirms the main purpose of a dialog. It is triggered by pressing `Enter` or `Ctrl+Enter` on Windows/Linux and `Enter` or `Cmd+Enter` on macOS. Note: Exception: if the focus is on an element that uses the `Enter` key, for example, a text area, the default button is triggered only by `Ctrl+Enter` on Windows/Linux and `Cmd+Enter` on macOS.

* The default button should always be present in a dialog. Only one button in a dialog can be the default one.

* If an action that a default button performs is dangerous, which means it can lead to data loss, there should always be an easy way to undo it. Otherwise, use a secondary button for a dangerous action and a default button for a safe action: ![A dialog with secondary and primary buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_merge_dialog.png)

#### Focused

!['Cancel' button in a focused state](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_focused.png)
All buttons can get focus, even on macOS if the
Full Keyboard Access
option is disabled in Preferences > Keyboard >
Shortcuts.
A focused button behavior varies on macOS/Linux and Windows.

macOS:

* A focused button is invoked by pressing `Space`. Focused and default buttons are independent, so when the focus moves from one button to another, the default button does not change.

* Make the second most popular button in the dialog focused. It’s recommended to have one default and one focused button so that most of the actions can be triggered using the keyboard.

* It’s recommended to have one default and one focused button so that most of the actions can be triggered using the keyboard.

Windows, Linux:

* The focused button is triggered by pressing `Enter` or `Space`. If a non-default button gets focus, the default button is invoked using `Ctrl+Enter`. On pressing the `Tab` key, the New Window button gets the focus and is triggered with `Enter` or `Space` . The original This Window button is triggered with `Ctrl+Enter`. If the focus moves to the control that’s not a button, the original default button is triggered by `Enter`.

Correct
![A dialog with buttons: 'New Window' (focused), 'Cancel', and 'This Window' (default).](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_open_project_dialog.png)
Incorrect
![A dialog with buttons: 'New Window', 'Cancel', and 'This Window' (default and focused).](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_open_project_dialog_incorrect.png)

#### Disabled

![Disabled button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_disabled.png)
Disable a button if:

* The control to which the button is related is disabled.

* Not all required fields in the dialog are filled.

Other [standard buttons](#common-buttons) are described below. They can be regular or default buttons.

#### Hover

On hovering over a button, show a tooltip with the shortcut and the action name if it can be clarified.
For more details,
see [Context help](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/context-help.html).

If the action is clear, show the shortcut only. If the action can be clarified, show the action name and the shortcut:

![Hovered buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_hovered.png)

### Common buttons

#### Apply

|                          ![Hovered buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_apply.png)                       |                         Use the Apply button in dialogs with many settings that affect how data is displayed. The                             Apply button                             allows you to save and preview the effect of the selected options and continue changing the                             settings, for example, change the editor color scheme in settings.                           The Apply should be [disabled](#disabled) if no changes have been made in the dialog.                                                 |

#### Cancel

|                          ![Hovered buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_cancel.png)                       |                             TheCancel button reverts the app to the state before the dialog was                                 invoked and works as an equivalent to the `Esc` key.                               If a confirmation button is present in a dialog, for example,                             OK or                             Save, it’s required to have the Cancel button.                               If it is not clear what will happen on clicking the Cancel button,                             make the label more [specific](#be-specific), for example, Continue Editing.                        |

#### Close

|                          ![Hovered buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_close.png)                       |                         Use the                             Close                             label only if nothing can be changed in the dialog and there is no confirmation button, for example, in                             the                             `Help \| My Productivity`                             dialog.                             In all other cases, use the                             Cancel                             button.                                                 |

#### Help

|                          ![Hovered buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/button_help.png)                       |                         The help button appears in the bottom-left corner of a dialog and                             opens a documentation website. Add this button if the dialog's functionality is described                             in documentation.                            |



# Built-In Button

A built-in button is an icon placed inside an input control.

![Built-in-button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/built_in_button.png)

### Implementation

To place a button inside a text field, use [ExtendableTextField](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/components/fields/ExtendableTextField.java) and
its `addExtension()` method.

## When to use

Use a built-in button instead of adding a separate [button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/button.html) on the right where possible to save space and declutter the interface:

| Correct ![Browse button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/built_in_button_browse_correct.png) |Incorrect ![Incorrect browse button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/built_in_button_browse_incorrect.png) |

### Browse

Use the Browse icon to select a single file or a folder from the disc.

![Browse](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/built_in_button_browse.png)
#### Implementation

A combo box with the Browse button:

Kotlin:

```KOTLIN
val browseExtension = ExtendableTextComponent.Extension.create(
    AllIcons.General.OpenDisk,
    AllIcons.General.OpenDiskHover,
    "Open file",
    { System.out.println("Browse file clicked") }
)
val extComboBox = ComboBox<String>(STRING_VALUES)
extComboBox.setEditable(true)
extComboBox.setEditor(object : BasicComboBoxEditor() {
  override fun createEditorComponent(): JTextField {
    val ecbEditor = ExtendableTextField()
    ecbEditor.addExtension(browseExtension)
    ecbEditor.setBorder(null)
    return ecbEditor
  }
})
```

Java:

```JAVA
ExtendableTextComponent.Extension browseExtension =
  ExtendableTextComponent.Extension.create(
    AllIcons.General.OpenDisk,
    AllIcons.General.OpenDiskHover,
    "Open file",
    () -> System.out.println("Browse file clicked")
  );
ComboBox<String> extComboBox = new ComboBox<>(STRING_VALUES);
extComboBox.setEditable(true);
extComboBox.setEditor(new BasicComboBoxEditor() {
  @Override
  protected JTextField createEditorComponent() {
    ExtendableTextField ecbEditor = new ExtendableTextField();
    ecbEditor.addExtension(browseExtension);
    ecbEditor.setBorder(null);
    return ecbEditor;
  }
});
```

### Expand a field

If the input text can be long and the place is constrained,
use an input field with the Expand button:

![Collapsed built-in button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/built_in_button_collapsed.png)
Expanded field:

![Expanded built-in button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/built_in_button_expanded.png)

### List values

Use the List icon to select a value from the list of objects such as classes, methods, or environment variables:

![List of values](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/built_in_button_list.png)

### Add value

Use the Add button to select multiple values, such as files, variables, folder paths. The selected values will be added to the existing list.

![Add a value to the field](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/built_in_button_add.png)

## When not to use

### Cut, Copy, Paste

Do not use the Copy, Paste or Cut button. Instead, make sure these actions are available on pressing `Cmd/Ctrl+X`, `Cmd/Ctrl+C`, and `Cmd/Ctrl+V` shortcuts or  from the context menu.

|      Correct     ![Browse button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/built_in_button_copy_correct.png)  |     Incorrect     ![Incorrect browse button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/built_in_button_copy_incorrect.png)  |

### Help, Info

Do not use the Help or Info buttons to open an external link or a hint. Use the [context help](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/context-help.html) instead.

| Correct ![Context help ](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/built_in_button_help_correct.png) |Incorrect ![Incorrect browse button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/built_in_button_help_incorrect.png) |

## Shortcut

The shortcut for a built-in button is `Shift+Enter`.
The shortcut activates only when the input field with the button is focused.



# Split Button

<tldr>
Implementation: [JBOptionButton](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/components/JBOptionButton.kt)
</tldr>

A split button is a combination of a regular [button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/button.html) and a drop-down button.

![Split button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/split_button.png)

## Anatomy

A split button consists of the main action on the left and a drop-down button that shows a dropdown
with less common actions on the right:

![Split button action anatomy](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/split_button_anatomy.png)

## When to use

### More than two related actions

When there are more than two actions related to the main action, and there is not enough space for separate buttons, put these actions into
the dropdown menu:

![Related actions in a split button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/split_button_related_actions.png)

### The second action is dangerous and uncommon

Dangerous actions can destroy users’ data and cannot be easily undone.
To avoid accidental clicks on a dangerous action, you can hide it in the dropdown menu if this action is uncommon, for example Force Push:

![Dangerous action in a split button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/split_button_dangerous_action.png)
An uncommon dangerous action can be the only action in the menu.

Note:
Uncommon actions are the actions called in rare cases for specific purposes. For example, the Force Push action, unlike the Commit and Push... action, is available under certain circumstances
and covers rare user scenarios. Thus, it can be considered as uncommon and hidden in the dropdown menu.

## When not to use

### Unrelated actions

If unrelated actions are hidden under the dropdown menu, they are hard to find:

Incorrect

![Unrelated actions](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/split_button_unrelated_actions.png)
Correct

![Unrelated actions in separate buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/split_button_unrelated_actions_correct.png)

### Only one related action

Putting the single action in the dropdown menu doesn't save a lot of space:

Incorrect

![One related action](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/split_button_one_action.png)
Correct

![Unrelated actions in separate buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/split_button_one_two_buttons.png)
Note:
Exception: If the action is [dangerous and uncommon](#the-second-action-is-dangerous-and-uncommon), you can put it in the menu.

## How to use

### Main action

Refer to the [regular button rules](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/button.html#how-to-use).

### Dropdown button

#### Click

* Show the dropdown menu with secondary actions.

* Hide the menu when clicking outside the menu or on the second dropdown button click.

#### Hover

Show a tooltip:

![Tooltip on hover](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/split_button_tooltip_on_hover.png)

### Dropdown menu

Place related actions into the dropdown menu. Do not duplicate the main action in the dropdown menu, otherwise it is confusing how to trigger the main action — with the button or from the menu.

Incorrect

![Duplicated actions in dropdown menu](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/split_button_duplicated_action.png)
Correct

![Unique actions in dropdown menu](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/split_button_related_actions.png)
If there is a dangerous action among other actions in the dropdown, add the line separators above and below it to lessen the chance of calling this action by mistake:

![Dangerous action in the dropdown menu](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/split_button_dangerous_action_separator.png)

## Keyboard navigation & shortcuts

* Trigger the main action when the [default](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/button.html#default) button shortcut is pressed if the split button is the default one.

* Open the dropdown menu with the first menu item selected on `Alt+Shift+Enter`.

* Do not show the dropdown menu when the button gains focus.

### Focus on the button

| `Space` |Invoke the main action. |
| `Arrow Down` |Show the dropdown menu with secondary actions and move focus to the first item in the menu. |
|          `Tab`           `Shift + Tab`        |Move focus to the control next to the split button and hide the dropdown menu. |

### Focus on the dropdown menu

|          `Enter`           `Space`        |Invoke the selected action. |
|          `Arrow Down`           `Arrow Up`        |           * Navigate through the elements.    * Pressing `Arrow Down` on the top element moves the focus to the bottom element.    * Pressing `Arrow Up` on the bottom element moves the focus to the top element.        |
| `Esc` |Close the dropdown menu and move the focus to the split button. |



# Checkbox

<tldr>
Implementation:
[JCheckBox](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/javax/swing/JCheckBox.html),
[JBCheckBox](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/components/JBCheckBox.java)
</tldr>

![A preview of checkboxes in different states](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox.png)

## When to use

Use checkboxes for yes/no choices or for selecting several items in a group:

![An example of a checkbox group with two selected options](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_when_to_use.png)

## When not to use

If only one option in a group can be selected, use [radio button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/radio-button.html):

|                      Incorrect                     ![A radio button group with only one selected option possible](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_when_not_to_use_1_incorrect.png)                  |                     Correct                     ![Two radio buttons with clear labels](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_when_not_to_use_1_correct.png)                  |

If the behavior in the "off" state is unclear from the checkbox label, use two [radio buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/radio-button.html) instead
and label them accordingly:

|                      Incorrect                     ![A radio button group with only one selected option possible](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_when_not_to_use_2_incorrect.png)                  |                     Correct                     ![Two radio buttons with clear labels](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_when_not_to_use_2_correct.png)                  |

## How to use

### Label on the right

A label accompanies each checkbox and is placed on the right side.

|                                  Correct![A correct checkbox with the label on the right](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_label_right_correct.png)                          |                                 Incorrect![An incorrect checkbox with the label on the left](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_label_right_incorrect.png)                          |

### Long labels

If a label is long, split it into two lines. Use HTML formatting for that. Avoid labels that take more than two lines. See recommendations on [writing concise labels](#writing-guidelines) below.

|                          Correct![A correct checkbox with the label on the right](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_label_long_correct.png)                      |                             Incorrect![An incorrect checkbox with the label on the left](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_label_long_incorrect.png)                      |

#### Implementation

Kotlin UI DSL:

```KOTLIN
checkBox(
    """<html>Insert selected suggestion by pressing space, dot,<br/>
or other context-dependent keys</html>""")
```

Java:

```JAVA
new JCheckBox(
"<html>Insert selected suggestion by pressing space, dot,<br/>" +
        "or other context-dependent keys</html>");
```

### Checkboxes in a table

If a checkbox appears in a table, place the label into the column header and do not repeat it on every
row:

![A table with checkboxes where the label is placed into the column header](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_when_to_use_3.png)
#### Implementation

Checkboxes are rendered in tables with [BooleanTableCellRenderer](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/core-ui/src/ui/BooleanTableCellRenderer.java)
and edited with `DefaultCellEditor(JCheckBox)` implementation.
For any column that should be rendered as a checkbox, set both a renderer and editor for consistency.
The type of data in the correspondent column of the `Table` model should either be `Boolean`
or `String` containing `true` or `false`.

```JAVA
TableColumn column = table.getColumnModel().getColumn(COLUMN_INDEX);
column.setCellEditor(JBTable.createBooleanEditor());
column.setCellRenderer(new BooleanTableCellRender());
```

### Three-state checkbox

#### Status of children

In a group of options, use the parent checkbox to show the status of its children. The state of the parent checkbox can be checked, indeterminate or unchecked. When a user clicks an indeterminate checkbox for the first time, the whole group becomes checked. The second click unchecks the whole group.

![Different states for a parent checkbox: checked, indeterminate, and unchecked](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_three_state.png)
##### Implementation

The three-state checkbox is represented by the [ThreeStateCheckBox](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/util/ui/src/com/intellij/util/ui/ThreeStateCheckBox.java)
class which represents its state with the `ThreeStateCheckBox.State` enum containing `SELECTED,
NOT_SELECTED, DONT_CARE` states.

#### Download status

An indeterminate checkbox can also show the download status. In the example below, a remote repository with Repositories "tools-base" and "contrib" are being loaded. When loading is finished, the indeterminate checkbox will be replaced with the checked checkbox if there are commits, or an unchecked checkbox if there are no commits.

![Indeterminate checkboxes showing download status](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_download_status.png)
##### Implementation

In a table, the three-state checkbox is represented by [ThreeStateCheckBoxRenderer](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/lang-impl/src/com/intellij/profile/codeInspection/ui/table/ThreeStateCheckBoxRenderer.java)
that provides both `TableCellRenderer` and `TableEditor`.
It accepts `Boolean` type in the column being supplied by the `TableModel` and
becomes `DONT_CARE` when the value in the cell is null.
Otherwise, it becomes `SELECTED` for `Boolean.TRUE`, and `NOT_SELECTED`
for `Boolean.FALSE`.

## Writing guidelines

Use sentence-style capitalization:
|                                          Correct![A correct checkbox with the imperative form of the verb](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_writing_1_correct.png)                                  |                                         Incorrect![An incorrect checkbox with the declarative form of the verb](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_writing_1_incorrect.png)                                  |

Do not use ending punctuation:
|                                          Correct![A correct checkbox with the imperative form of the verb](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_writing_2_correct.png)                                  |                                         Incorrect![An incorrect checkbox with the declarative form of the verb](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_writing_2_incorrect.png)                                  |

Use the imperative form of verbs:
|                                          Correct![A correct checkbox with the imperative form of the verb](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_writing_3_correct.png)                                  |                                         Incorrect![An incorrect checkbox with the declarative form of the verb](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_writing_3_incorrect.png)                                  |

Do not use negation in labels as it complicates understanding:
|                                          Correct![A correct checkbox with the imperative form of the verb](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_writing_4_correct.png)                                  |                                         Incorrect![An incorrect checkbox with the declarative form of the verb](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/checkbox_writing_4_incorrect.png)                                  |

Note:
Exception: Do not show again checkbox.

Make labels short and intelligible. See [Writing short and clear](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/writing-short.html).

## How to layout

Follow the guidelines for [checkboxes and radio buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/layout.html#checkboxes-and-radio-buttons) layout.



# Combo Box

<tldr>
Implementation: [ComboBox](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/openapi/ui/ComboBox.java)
</tldr>

A combo box combines a [drop down list](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/drop-down.html) and an [input field](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/input-field.html), allowing the user to select a value from the list or enter a custom value.

![A preview of a combo box](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/combobox.png)

Use [ComboBox](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/openapi/ui/ComboBox.java) instead of `javax.swing.JComboBox`.
To make combo box editable invoke:

```JAVA
comboBox.setEditable(true);
```

## When to use

### Select value or enter custom

When the user needs to select a value or enter a custom value, use the combo box:

![A font size  that allows selecting predefined values as well as entering a custom value](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/combobox_when_to_use_1.png)

### Return to previous states

Use a combo box if users may need to revisit previous values, such as saving entered paths for quick selection later:

![A  with an open menu with previously selected values](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/combobox_when_to_use_2.png)

## When not to use

### The number of options is finite

If the number of options is finite, and there is no need to enter custom values, use a [dropdown list](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/drop-down.html) or [radio buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/radio-button.html):

![The Theme dropdown with a predefined list of values](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/combobox_when_not_to_use_1.png)

### Impossible to list values

If it is not possible to list the most likely choices, use an [input field](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/input-field.html) instead:

![A port number input](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/combobox_when_not_to_use_2.png)

### Large list with expected values

If the list is big, and the user knows what value they need and won’t review the list, use an input field with completion:

![An input field with a completion popup](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/combobox_when_not_to_use_3.png)

## How to use

### Label and default value

For the [label](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/drop-down.html#label) and the [default value](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/drop-down.html#default-value) apply the same rules as for the
[dropdown list](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/drop-down.html).

### Initial state

If there are no values in the list initially, replace the combo box with an input field.
This way, users won't waste their time clicking the empty combo box to find out that there are no options available.

|        Incorrect![An incorrect example of a repository input field without values](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/combobox_how_to_use_1_incorrect.png)      |       Correct![A correct example of a repository input field without values](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/combobox_how_to_use_1_correct.png)      |

Replace the input field with a combo box after a value has been entered and confirmed:

|        Incorrect![An incorrect example of a repository input field without values](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/combobox_how_to_use_2_incorrect.png)      |       Correct![A correct example of a repository input field without values](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/combobox_how_to_use_2_correct.png)      |

### Menu items

#### Predefined options

Show the predefined or most likely options in the list. Follow the rules for [dropdown menu items](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/drop-down.html#menu-items).

#### Previous inputs

If the user needs to return to previous inputs, add such values to the end of the list when the confirmation button in the dialog is clicked:

![A combo box with previously entered values in the menu](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/combobox_menu_items_1.png)

#### Built-in button

Use [built-in buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/built-in-button.html) to add values or expand the combo box, e.g., the browse button:

![A combo box with the browse built-in button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/combobox_menu_items_2.png)

## Validation

If the user enters an invalid value, highlight the combo box with red and show an error message in a tooltip. For
more details, see [validation errors](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/validation-errors.html).

![A combo box with an error message](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/combobox_validation.png)

## How to layout

Follow the [labeled input controls](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/layout.html#labeled-input-controls).

## Built-in behaviour

### Opening the menu

The combo box menu opens by clicking on the arrow button on the right or pressing the `Down` arrow key when the combo box is focused.
The menu opens down by default. If there is not enough space, the menu opens up.

### Selected value

The value that was shown in the closed combo box is selected in the open menu. A value in the list is not selected if a custom value was entered.

### Moving the selection

The selection is moved and the value in the combo box is updated by pressing the Up and Down arrow keys. When using a mouse, the selection is changed on mouse hover, the value is updated by clicking the mouse button or pressing `Enter`.

### Closing the menu

The menu remains opened until the user clicks the item in the list, presses `Enter` or `Esc`, clicks outside the menu,
or switches to another app.



# Context Help

Use context help to briefly explain how a functionality works if it is not clear from the UI or the application behavior. A full description of the functionality should be provided in [product web help](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/).

Context help can be shown as an [inline help text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/inline-help-text.html), in a [help tooltip](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/tooltip.html), and in an [empty state](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/empty-state.html).

## Inline help text

Use an [inline help text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/inline-help-text.html) in settings dialogs that are not constrained by space and are not frequently used. Since settings are rarely changed, users may forget their purpose, so displaying the information immediately makes sense.

![Context help in an inline text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/context_help_inline_text.png)

## Tooltip

Use a [tooltip](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/tooltip.html):

* If the space is not enough for showing the inline help text.

* In frequently used dialogs, tool windows, or popups. The more often a person uses an interface, the more likely they are to remember what each option does.

* For icons or other controls that do not have a label.

![Context help in a tooltip](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/context_help_tooltip.png)

## Empty state

Fill in [empty states](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/empty-state.html) of tool windows, tables, trees, and other containers with:

* a reason why the data is missing

* an action that can fix it

* a link to a corresponding article in the web help.

![Empty state of a tool window](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_structure.png)

## When to use

Below you will find rules for [tooltips](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/tooltip.html) and [inline texts](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/inline-help-text.html).

|        ![Explain a setting](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/context_help_explain.png)      |         Explain complex behavior that a short action or a setting name cannot convey clearly.        |
|        ![Input format requirements](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/context_help_input_format.png)      |         Provide input format requirements and examples.        |
|        ![Suggest alternative ways](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/context_help_alternatives.png)      |         Suggest alternative ways.        |
|        ![Warn about possible issues](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/context_help_input_warning.png)      |         Warn about possible issues.        |
|        ![Explain limitations](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/context_help_limitation.png)      |         Explain limitations.        |
|        ![Provide quick navigation to related settings](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/context_help_navigation.png)      |         Provide quick navigation to related settings.        |
|        ![Explain IDE-specific entities](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/context_help_terms.png)      |         Explain IDE-specific entities.        |

## When not to use

### Do not explain UI

Do not use context help to explain how the user interface works. If you need to explain that, consider redesigning the UI.

|        Correct       ![Don't explain how UI elements should work](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/context_help_explain_ui_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Incorrect UI requires additional explanation](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/context_help_explain_ui_incorrect.png)      |

### Do not explain common actions

Do not explain common actions and entities. Show a regular tooltip with an action name and shortcut in this case.

|        Correct       ![Don't explain common actions](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/context_help_explain_simple_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Common actions are explained in the tooltip](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/context_help_explain_simple_incorrect.png)      |

### Do not clutter UI with context help

Do not explain each option. Too many help icons or too much inline text make a dialog cluttered and harder to navigate visually.
If all options need to be explained, consider rewriting the labels to make them clearer.

|        Correct       ![Don't explain every option](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/context_help_explain_too_many_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Every option has its tooltip](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/context_help_explain_too_many_incorrect.png)      |

## How to use

See [Inline help text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/inline-help-text.html), [Tooltip](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/tooltip.html), and [Empty State](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/empty-state.html).



# Inline Help Text

Inline help texts provide useful information about settings:

![Inline help text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/context_help_inline_text.png)

## When to use

Follow the rules for [context help](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/context-help.html).

## How to use

### Text length

Show no more than five lines of help text to not clutter the screen.
Text width is limited to 70 characters.
![Inline text height](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline_text_height.png)
Show more than five lines only when a text cannot be shortened for legal purposes.

![Inline text legal](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline_text_legal.png)
#### Implementation

```KOTLIN
panel {
  row {
    checkBox("Send usage statistics when using EAP versions")
      .comment("""
        <p>Help JetBrains improve its products by sending anonymous
        data about features and plugins used, hardware and software
        configuration, statistics on types of files, number of files
        per project, etc.</p>
        <br/>
        <p>Please note that this will not include personal data or
        any sensitive information, such as source code, file names,
        etc. The data sent complies with the
        <a href=\"https://www.jetbrains.com\">
        JetBrains Privacy Policy</a></p>
        """.trimIndent()
      )
  }
}
```

### Links

Provide a [link](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/link.html) to the corresponding help article or to a place in the IDE where the related settings can be found.
Place the link at the end of the text where possible so that it does not disrupt reading.

|        Internal link       ![Internal link](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline_text_internal_link.png)      |       External link       ![External link](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline_text_external_link.png)      |

### Text style formatting

#### Avoid highlighting

Avoid text highlighting. Usually, the help text is short, and no highlighting in bold or italics is needed:
|        Correct       ![Avoid highlighting: correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline_text_formatting_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Avoid highlighting: incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline_text_formatting_incorrect.png)      |

#### Avoid brackets

Avoid using brackets in control labels and place this information in the inline text instead:
|        Correct       ![Avoid brackets: correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline_text_brackets_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Avoid brackets: incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline_text_brackets_incorrect.png)      |

### Writing guidelines

* Make help text [short and descriptive](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/writing-short.html).

* Do not repeat the setting name in the help text:

|        Correct       ![Avoid brackets: correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline_text_repetition_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Avoid brackets: incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline_text_repetition_incorrect.png)      |

## Placement

### Labeled inputs, checkboxes, radio buttons, and buttons

Place the help text to the right of labeled inputs (fields, combo boxes, or text areas), checkboxes, buttons, or radio buttons if all the following applies:

* The space to the right is empty.

* The help text has 1–5 words, not counting articles and prepositions.

* The control label has 1–5 words.

Labeled inputs:

![Input fields with inline texts on the right](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline_text_on_the_right_input_field.png)
#### Implementation

```KOTLIN
panel {
  row("Plugin update policy:") {
      comboBox(listOf("Default", "Non default"))
      comment("Ignore by Maven 3+")
  }
  row("Thread count:") {
      textField()
      comment("-T option")
  }
}
```

Checkboxes:

![Checkboxes with inline texts on the right](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline_text_on_the_right_checkbox.png)
#### Implementation

```KOTLIN
panel {
  row {
    checkBox("Build project automatically")
    comment("Works while not running / debugging")
  }
  row {
    checkBox("Compile independent modules in parallel")
    comment("May require larger heap size")
  }
}
```

Buttons:

![Button with inline texts on the right](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline_text_on_the_right_button.png)

In other cases, place the help text under the UI controls:

![Input filed with inline text on the bottom](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline_text_on_the_bottom.png)
#### Implementation

```KOTLIN
panel {
  row("Default directory:") {
    textFieldWithBrowseButton()
      .comment(
        "Preselected in Open and New | Project dialogs"
      )
  }
}
```

If there is no space under the UI control, use the [help tooltip](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/tooltip.html#question-mark-icon-for-help-tooltips) with the question mark icon for labeled inputs, checkboxes, and radio buttons.
For buttons, use the help tooltip without the icon.

### Trees, lists, and tables

#### Text applies to the whole component

If the help text applies to a whole list, tree, or table, place it below the control.
![Inline text under the table](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline_text_under_table.png)
##### Implementation

```KOTLIN

import javax.swing.JTable

panel {
  row {
    cell(createTable()) // Actual table creation
      .align(Align.FILL)
      .comment("""
        &lt;Project> is content roots of all modules,
        all immediate descendants<br/>of the projects base
        directory, and .idea directory contents
        """.trimIndent()
      )
  }.resizableRow()
}
```

#### Text applies to a single item

If the help text applies to a single list, tree, or table item, its location will depend on its length.
##### Short texts

Place short texts (1–10 words) to the right of the item:
![Inline text under the table](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline_text_on_the_right_tree.png)

##### Long texts

* Place longer texts (more than 10 words) into the detail part of master-detail layouts:

![Inline text on the bottom of the master detail layout](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline_text_on_the_bottom_master_detail.png)
* For other cases, use the [help tooltip](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/tooltip.html#question-mark-icon-for-help-tooltips) with the question mark icon:

![Inline text on the bottom of the master detail layout](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_list.png)

### Group of controls

If the help text applies to several UI controls, place it at the bottom of the group.

![Inline text for a group of controls](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline_text_group.png)
#### Implementation

Use [Panel.group()](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-impl/src/com/intellij/ui/dsl/builder/Panel.kt) as the border for panels that need title and possibly the gray line on the right of the title:

```KOTLIN
panel {
  group("Build and Run") {
    row("Build and run with:") {
      comboBox(listOf("IntelliJ IDEA", "Gradle"))
    }
    row("Run tests with:") {
      comboBox(listOf("IntelliJ IDEA", "Gradle"))
    }
    row {
      comment("""
        <p>By default IntelliJ IDEA uses Gradle to build the project
        and run the tasks.</p>
        <p>In a pure Java/Kotlin project, building and running
        by means of IDE might be faster, thanks to optimizations.
        Note, that the IDE doesn't support all Gradle plugins and
        the project might not be built correctly with some of them.</p>
        """.trimIndent()
      )
    }
  }
  group("Gradle") {
    row("Use Gradle from:") {
      comboBox(gradleModel)
    }
  }
}
```

You can find more examples by invoking the Tools | Internal Actions | UI | Kotlin UI DSL | UI DSL Showcase action (available in [internal mode](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/enabling-internal.html) and clicking the View source links on specific pages.



# Tooltip

<tldr>
Implementation: [HelpTooltip](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ide/HelpTooltip.java)
</tldr>

A tooltip appears on hovering over a UI element and shows an action name or provides useful information about an action or a setting.

![Tooltip](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_main.png)

## When to use

There are three types of tooltips:

|          ![Action tooltip](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_action.png)      |         Action          Shows an action name or label for icons and unlabeled controls such as main toolbar widgets, and a shortcut if available.           Required: action name           Optional: shortcut        |
|          ![Action help tooltip](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_help_action.png)      |         Action help          Shows help text for icons and unlabeled controls in addition to an action name or label.           Required: action name, help text           Optional: shortcut, link        |
|          ![Help tooltip](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_help.png)      |         Help         Shows help text for all other controls. It is shown on hovering the [question mark icon](#question-mark-icon-for-help-tooltips).           Required: help text. Action name or label is not required because it is shown in the UI.           Optional: shortcut, link.        |

All icons and unlabeled controls should have an Action or an Action help tooltip.

Use Action help and Help tooltips according to the [Context help](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/context-help.html) rules.

## How to use

### Shortcut

* Always show a shortcut if an action or a setting has one.

* Do not show a single shortcut in a tooltip:

|              Correct             ![A tooltip with a shortcut](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_shortcut_correct.png)          |             Incorrect             ![A tooltip with a shortcut but without the action name](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_shortcut_incorrect.png) |

### Link

* Provide a link to a source that can further explain the action or the setting. A link can navigate to a place in the IDE or to an external help article:

|              Internal link             ![A tooltip with an internal link](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_internal_link.png)          |             External link             ![A tooltip with an external link](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_external_link.png)          |

* Do not show just an action name and a link to a help article. Provide help text so that the user does not need to switch to a web browser:

|              Correct             ![A tooltip with a link and help text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_link_correct.png)          |             Incorrect             ![A tooltip with a link but without help text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_link_incorrect.png) |

### Text length

The text width in an action tooltip is not limited. The text width in a help tooltip is limited by 250px.

Show no more than 10 lines of help text. If the text does not fit, leave only the essential information and add a link to a help article.

|              Correct             ![A tooltip with a long help text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_text_length_correct.png)          |             Incorrect             ![A tooltip with a too long help text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_text_length_incorrect.png) |

If the help text is longer than 5 lines, separate the text into paragraphs with the `<p>` tag. The `<p>` tag adds vertical space between paragraphs to visually separate them. Do not use the `<br/>` tag as it does not add space.

#### Implementation

Kotlin:

```KOTLIN
val LONG_TEXT = """A new overloading method will be created with
    the new parameter added to this method definition.<p>
    The method with the old signature will be kept and the call
    to the new method will be added to it. The necessary value
    or expression will be passed to the new method call."""
HelpTooltip().setDescription(LONG_TEXT).installOn(component)
```

Java:

```JAVA
String LONG_TEXT = "A new overloading method will be created with " +
    "the new parameter added to this method definition.<p>" +
    "The method with the old signature will be kept and the call " +
    "to the new method will be added to it. The necessary value " +
    "or expression will be passed to the new method call.";
new HelpTooltip().setDescription(LONG_TEXT).installOn(component);
```

### Text style formatting

Avoid using style formatting in the help text. Usually, the text is short and no bold or italics are needed.

|              Correct             ![Text without formatting](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_text_formatting_correct.png)          |             Incorrect             ![Text with formatting](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_text_formatting_incorrect.png) |

### Writing guidelines

* Make the help text [short and descriptive](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/writing-short.html).

* In a help tooltip, do not repeat an action or a setting name in the text:

|              Correct             ![Text is not repeated](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_writing_correct.png)          |             Incorrect             ![Text repetition in the checkbox and the tooltip](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_writing_incorrect.png) |

### Question mark icon for help tooltips

Always use the help tooltip with the question mark icon. Without the icon, it is unclear which component has help information.

Always place the question mark icon to the right of the corresponding UI component.

Examples with different controls:

#### Checkbox

![Checkbox](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_checkbox.png)

#### Tree item

![Tree item](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_tree.png)

#### Labeled input

![Labeled input](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_labeled_input.png)

#### Group header

![Group header](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_group_header.png)

#### Settings breadcrumbs

![Settings breadcrumbs](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_settings_header.png)

#### Button

![Button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_button.png)
Exception: do not use the help tooltip with buttons at a dialog’s bottom.
Put the information into the help article that is opened with the question mark button in the bottom left corner.

|              Correct             ![Button in the dialog footer](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_footer_correct.png)          |             Incorrect             ![Button in the dialog footer with the incorrect help icon](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tooltip_footer_incorrect.png) |

## Built-in behavior

All tooltips appear on hover (not on click), including the help tooltip with the question mark icon.

All tooltips are hidden when the mouse cursor leaves the area that triggers the tooltip.

If the mouse cursor stays in the tooltip trigger area, tooltips are also hidden after a timeout specified in the table below.

|          Tooltip      |         Appears after      |         Hides after           If the cursor is in the tooltip trigger area        |
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
|          Action      |         500 milliseconds           ide.tooltip.initialReshowDelay registry key        |         10 seconds           ide.helptooltip.regular.dismissDelay        |
|          Action help      |      |         30 seconds           ide.helptooltip.full.dismissDelay        |
|          Help      |      |         Never hides      |

If a tooltip has a link, it is possible to move the mouse cursor over the tooltip. The tooltip does not close automatically when the cursor is over it.

Tooltips are positioned automatically depending on the mouse cursor location.



# Empty State

<tldr>
Implementation: [ComponentWithEmptyText](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/util/ui/ComponentWithEmptyText.java)
</tldr>

Empty states of tool windows, lists, trees, tables, master-detail layouts, or other container components should be informative for the users.
Fill in the empty states with the following:

* [A reason why the container is empty](#reason-why-empty)

* [Actions to fill in the area](#actions-to-fill-the-area)

* [A link to the corresponding help topic](#help-topic)

![Empty state of a tool window](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_structure.png)

## Reason why empty

### Explain the current state

The default pattern is `No [entity] added.` If `added`, `created`, `configured`, or other words act as synonyms in a particular case, use `added` for consistency.

|        Correct       ![Correct text in the empty state](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_reason_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Incorrect text in the empty state](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_reason_incorrect.png)      |

### Be precise

Do not introduce new entities that are not used in the current context.
Instead, use the terms from the current UI so that the user understands
what exactly is missing:

|        Correct       ![The reason is clear](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_clear_reason.png)      |       Incorrect       ![The reason is not clear](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_unclear_reason.png) |

## Actions to fill the area

An action makes it easier to understand what to start with
instead of searching for the appropriate icon on the toolbar.
It can also educate about the shortcut.

### Use one or two actions

Three or more actions would make it harder to choose what to start from.

|        Correct       ![One action](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_actions_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Three actions](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_actions_incorrect.png)      |

In rare cases, when you need to list all possible starting points, use the list layout.

If there is enough space (for example, in horizontal tool windows), you may use the table layout to place action links, shortcuts, and action descriptions:
![Table layout for actions](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_table.png)

### Open menus from the toolbar

If an action opens a toolbar menu, open it at the same position where it
would be opened with the corresponding toolbar button. This would explain
which toolbar icon opens the menu.

|        Correct       ![Toolbar menu](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_menu_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Menu under the action](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_menu_incorrect.png)      |

### Explain what to do when there is no action`

If there is no action that can be performed by clicking a link,
add a text describing all the required steps:

![Explain what to do when there is no action](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_no_actions.png)

### Hide the toolbar

Hide the area's toolbar if it does not have the same action as
in the empty state. Usually, all other toolbar actions are not
relevant in this case.

Correct

![Hide the toolbar for the empty state](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_no_actions.png)
Incorrect

![Toolbar is not needed](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_toolbar.png)

## Help topic

|        ![Link to a help topic](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_link_to_help.png)      |     Link to a help topic     In tool windows and [master-detail layouts](#empty-state-of-the-master-detail-layout), provide a link to a help topic that explains the functionality. Add the question mark icon in the beginning.        |
|        ![Inline hint under the table](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_inline_help.png)      |       Context help in inline hints       In tables, trees, and lists, provide instructions according to the [inline text help](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/context-help.html#inline-help-text) rules.  Avoid using question mark links in these cases because such components rarely require deep explanations.    |

## Empty state of the master-detail layout

Master-detail layouts include a list or a tree on the left (in the master part)
and the details area on the right.

* If the master area is empty, display the explanation, action, and link to the help article.

* If the details area is empty, no explanations are needed. In this case, show the actions to fill in the area.

![Empty master-detail layout](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_master_detail_layout.png)

## Writing guidelines

### Punctuation

Separate sentences in the empty state with periods, but do not put a period after the action link.
Use the ellipses at the end of the action link if this link opens a dialog or a popup which requires some input from the user.

|        Correct       ![Correct punctuation in the empty state](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_punctuation_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Incorrect punctuation in the empty state](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_punctuation_incorrect.png)      |

### Capitalization

Use sentence capitalization in the empty state texts and links.

|        Correct       ![Correct capitalization in the empty state](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_capitalization_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Incorrect capitalization in the empty state](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_capitalization_incorrect.png)      |

### Avoid excessive verbs

* In actions, avoid words that describe physical actions like `press` or `click` — they are obvious from how the link works.

* Avoid saying `add new`. Just use `add` because all that is added is new in the context of an empty UI area.
