|        Correct       ![Correct usage of verbs in the empty state](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_verbs_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Incorrect usage of verbs in the empty state](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_verbs_incorrect.png)      |

## Sizes and placement

Vertical spacing:

![Empty state vertical spacing](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_vertical_spacing.png)
Minimum right and left margins:

![Empty state horizontal spacing](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_horizontal_spacing.png)
Use non-breaking spaces in the following cases:

* Between action names and shortcuts

* For articles and prepositions

|        Correct       ![Correct usage of non-breaking spaces in the empty state](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_non_breaking_space_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Incorrect usage of non-breaking spaces in the empty state](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_non_breaking_space_incorrect.png)      |



# Description Text

Description text provides explanatory information about a set of settings or a single item in a list or tree.

![01 description text example](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/01_description_text_example.png)

## When to Use

Use description text to:

* Show details about items in a list or tree:

![02 use in tree](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/02_use_in_tree.png)
* Describe a group of settings:

![03 use in settings](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/03_use_in_settings.png)

## How to Use

### Text

Follow general rules in [Writing short and clear](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/writing-short.html) and [Punctuation](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/punctuation.html).

Use the default text style for plain text. Increase line height by 3px from the default value.

Use [H4 bold](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/typography.html) (Default bold) for headings or to highlight important words:

![04 bold header](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/04_bold_header.png)
Use the editor font to highlight code snippets:

![05 editor font](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/05_editor_font.png)
Use bullets for lists:

![06 bullets](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/06_bullets.png)
Limit the width of the line to 70–80 symbols, as it is not convenient to read very long lines:

Incorrect

![07 width incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/07_width_incorrect.png)
Correct

![07 width correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/07_width_correct.png)
If the text does not fit, add a scrollbar:

![08 scroll](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/08_scroll.png)

### Appearance

Do not add borders around the description text. Use the panel color for the background.

| Incorrect |Correct |
----------------------
| ![09 frame incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/09_frame_incorrect.png) |![09 frame correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/09_frame_correct.png) |

For [links](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/link.html), use the default link color: `Link.activeForeground`. Underline links on hover:

![10 link](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/10_link.png)

### Insets

Separate the text from the surroundings with insets.

Use a 12px horizontal inset if the description text’s area has other elements:

![11 insets 12](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/11_insets_12.png)
Increase inset up to 20px if the description text is the only element:

![11 insets 20](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/11_insets_20.png)



# Drop-Down List

<tldr>
Implementation: [ComboBox](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/openapi/ui/ComboBox.java)
</tldr>

A drop-down list is a control that displays a list of choices on click and allows selecting one option.

![Example of a Theme drop-down with options: Light (selected in light), Dark (selected in dark), Light with Light Header, High Contrast, Darcula, and an option to get more themes](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown.png)

## When to use

### Single option

Use when a single option should be selected.

![Interface language drop-down with options: English (selected), German, Dutch, Chinese (Simplified), and an option to get more languages](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_when_to_1.png)
When multiple selections are possible, use [checkboxes](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/checkbox.html).

### Options are objects or states

The possible choices are objects or states.

![Output level drop-down with options: Debug, Info (selected), Warn, Error, and Warning](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_when_to_2.png)
When options are actions, use a menu or a [split button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/split-button.html).

### More than four options

The number of options is more than four.

![Regions drop-down with options: Africa, Americas, Asia except China Mainland, Europe (selected), Middle East, Oceania](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_when_to_3.png)
When there are four options or fewer, use [radio buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/radio-button.html).

### Space is limited

The screen space is limited, so there is not enough room for [radio buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/radio-button.html).

![Settings | Appearence dialog that has a complex layout with multiple drop-downs: Theme, Zoom, and Custom font](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_when_to_4.png)

### Default value is the most used

The default value is recommended for most users. A drop-down is a good way to hide unpopular alternatives.

In the example below a drop-down is used because Subpixels is the most popular choice. Using [radio-buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/radio-button.html)  puts all options on the same level of importance or popularity.

![Antialiasing drop-down with options: Subpixels (selected), Greyscale, Not antialiasing](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_when_to_5.png)

### Combined controls

If a control combines various UI elements as one setting, use a drop-down even if there are four options or fewer:

![Combined control with a checkbox 'Automatically check updated for' and a drop-down with 'Early access program' selected, following by a button 'Check now'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_when_to_6.png)

## When not to use

### Four or less options

If there are four options or fewer, use [radio buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/radio-button.html).

|        Correct       !['Open project in' radio group with options: 'New window', 'Current window', and 'Ask'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_when_not_to_3_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       !['Open project in' drop-down with options: 'New window' (selected), 'Current window', and 'Ask'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_when_not_to_3_incorrect.png)      |

### Multiple selection

If multiple selection is possible, use [checkboxes](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/checkbox.html).

|        Correct       !['UI Options' checkbox group with options: 'Smooth scrolling' (checked), 'Display icons in menu items' (checked), and 'Enable mnemonics in menu'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_when_not_to_1_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       !['UI Options' drop-down with options: 'Smooth scrolling' (checked), 'Display icons in menu items' (checked), and 'Enable mnemonics in menu'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_when_not_to_1_incorrect.png)      |

For a [single selection](#single-option) use a drop-down.

### List of actions

If there is a list of actions, use a menu or a [split button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/split-button.html).

|        Correct       ![Split-button 'Commit' and options: 'Commit and Push', 'Commit and Push Silently' (focused), and 'Create Patch'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_when_not_to_2_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Drop-down 'Commit' with options: 'Commit' (focused), 'Commit and Push', 'Commit and Push Silently', and 'Create Patch'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_when_not_to_2_incorrect.png)      |

For a list of [objects or states](#options-are-objects-or-states), use a drop-down.

### Adding values

If users may need to enter a value not currently in the list, use a [combo box](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/combo-box.html).

|        Correct       ![A combo box for selecting font size and entering a custom value is open, displaying options ranging from 20 to 72. The current selection is 20](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_when_not_to_4_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![A dropdown menu for selecting font size is open, displaying options ranging from 20 to 72. The current selection is 20](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_when_not_to_4_incorrect.png)      |

### On a toolbar

If a drop-down appears on a toolbar, use [toolbar drop-down](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/toolbar-drop-down.html) instead.

|        Correct       ![Run/debug widget in the main toolbar with multiple icon buttons, and a toolbar drop-down with selected 'StandAlone' option](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_when_not_to_5_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Run/debug widget in the main toolbar with multiple icon buttons, and a drop-down with selected 'StandAlone' option](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_when_not_to_5_incorrect.png)      |

## How to use

### Label

Follow the rules for the [input field](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/input-field.html#label).

![Drop-down menu labeled 'Placement' with the selected option set to 'Left'.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_1.png)

### Default value

Select the most likely or the safest value by default. In the example below the safest value is Ask, the behavior will not be unexpected to users:

![Drop-down menu labeled 'Insert imports on paste' with options 'All', 'Ask', and 'None'. The selected option set to 'Ask'.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_2.png)
Do not use an empty value as the default value. If no values are added to a drop-down yet, replace it with a button to add values.

|        Correct       ![Secondary button 'Add Settings Repository' which opens a dialog](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_3_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Drop-down 'Repository' with no selected option](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_3_incorrect.png)      |

### Menu items

#### Capitalization

Use [sentence-style capitalization](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/capitalization.html#sentence) for each menu item.

|        Correct       ![Drop-down menu labeled 'Default browser' with options 'System default', 'First listed', and 'Custom path'. The selected option set to 'System default'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_4_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Drop-down menu labeled 'Default browser' with options 'System Default', 'First Listed', and 'Custom Path'. The selected option set to 'System Default'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_4_incorrect.png)      |

#### No repeated words in items

Avoid repeating words in drop-down list items. Move repeating words to the label or after the drop-down.

|        Correct       ![Drop-down menu labeled 'Refresh every \[selection\] minutes' with options '10', '15', and '30'. The selected option set to '10'](images/dropdown_how_to_5_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Drop-down menu labeled 'Refresh every' with options '10 minutes', '15 minutes', and '30 minutes'. The selected option set to '10 minutes'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_5_incorrect.png)      |

#### Sorting items

Sort items in one of the following orders:

|        ![Drop-down menu labeled 'Placement' with options 'Left', 'Top', 'Right', and 'Bottom'. The selected option set to 'Top'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_6_1.png)      |       Logical order, for example, in a spatial relationship.        |
|        ![Drop-down menu labeled 'Global SQL dialect' with options '<None>', '<Generic SQL>', 'ClickHouse', 'DB2', 'Derby', 'Exasol', and other options available when scrolling. The selected option set to '<None>'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_6_2.png)      |       Alphabetical or numeric order if the options are equivalent to make it easier to find items.        |
|        ![Drop-down menu labeled 'Global encoding' with multiple options grouped in two groups and divided: popular options and the rest](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_6_3.png)      |       Place the most common options first. If there are more than 10 options, separate the most popular options with a line.         Sort the remaining items in alphabetical or numeric order.        |

#### Grouping

Group related items using separators. Add group headers if possible.

|              With dividers             ![Drop-down menu labeled 'Version' with options ranging from 1.5 to 1.9, and a meta-option 'Same as language version'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_7_1.png)          |             With a divider and group headers             ![Drop-down menu labeled 'Scheme' with two groups of options that have group titles and divided by a divider'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_7_2.png)          |

#### Actions related to a drop-down

If there are actions related to the drop-down, put them under the gear icon on the right:

![Drop-down menu 'Color Scheme' followed by a Settings icon-button related to the drop-down](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_8.png)

#### Meta-options

Note:
Meta-option is a special choice that controls how selections behave rather than being a specific value.

Enclose meta-options in pointy brackets and place them at the beginning of the list when they're important or popular options. In other cases, place them at the end of the list.

![Drop-down menu labeled 'Run tests with' with options 'Platform test runner', 'Gradle test runner', and ''. The selected option set to ''](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_9.png)
Do not assign special meanings to numeric or string values, use meta-options instead. It can be unclear that either 0 or an empty string are used to disable an option.

|              Correct             ![Drop-down menu labeled 'Version' with options ranging from 1.5 to 1.9, and a meta-option 'Same as language version'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_10_correct.png)          |             Incorrect             ![Drop-down menu labeled 'Version' with options ranging from 1.5 to 1.9, and an option '0'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_10_incorrect.png)          |

#### 'None' in simple layouts

Replace the <None> option with a checkbox if it doesn't make the layout more complex.

|              Correct             ![Checkbox 'Show close button at' followed by two radio buttons 'Right' and 'Left'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_11_correct.png)          |             Incorrect             ![Drop-down 'Close button position' with options 'Left', 'Right', '<None>'. The selected options is '<None>'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_11_incorrect.png)          |

#### Use icons and font formatting

|        ![Drop-down 'Run on' with multiple options that have icons related to their meanings](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_12_1.png)      |       Add icons to the values if they're well-known.        |
|        ![Drop-down 'Font' with multiple options that are showed in different fonts](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_12_2.png)      |       Use font formatting for a list of fonts. It will help users make a choice.        |

#### Default and changed values

|        ![Drop-down 'Editor color scheme' with multiple options. Option 'Light (Theme default)' has 'Light' in blue color and 'Theme default' in grey color](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_13_2.png)      |           * Use a blue font for values changed from the default.    * Use a secondary text to mark an option as default.        |

#### Submenus are not supported

Submenus are not supported for the drop-down list. Use a tree view instead

![Drop-down 'Keymap' with multiple options in a tree view showing dependencies in options](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dropdown_how_to_14.png)

## Built-in behaviour

### Opening the menu

A drop-down menu opens on clicking the drop-down button anywhere or pressing the `Down` key when the drop-down is
focused.

The menu opens down by default. If there is not enough space, the menu opens up.

### Selected value

When the menu opens, the default option (displayed when the menu is closed) is selected.

### Moving the selection

Selection in the menu is moved by pressing `Up` and `Down` keys when an item is hovered. Selection is moved as well when hovering the cursor over an item but it doesn't update the value.

### Closing the menu

The menu remains opened until the user selects an item, clicks outside the menu, presses the `Esc` key, or switches to another app.

### Single-click activation

A dropdown should work with a single mouse click:

1. Clicking to open a drop-down.

2. Hover over an item to select it.

3. Release the mouse to confirm the selection and close the dropdown.

## How to layout

Follow the [labeled input controls](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/layout.html#labeled-input-controls) guideline.



# Got It Tooltip

<tldr>
Implementation: [GotItTooltip](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-impl/src/com/intellij/ui/GotItTooltip.kt)

Related: ["Got It" Notification](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/informing-users.html#gotIt)
</tldr>

A Got It tooltip informs users about a new or changed behavior and provides a short summary of the change.

![Got it](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it.png)

## Structure

![Got it structure](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_structure.png)
### Body text

Always add the body text.  Shortly describe what the tooltip is showing.

Don't use body text as a title.

|        Correct![Got it body correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_body_correct.png)      |       Incorrect![Got it body incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_body_incorrect.png)      |

### Title

Add a header if the body text is 2 lines and more. A header should be short and quickly explain what a tooltip is about.

|        Correct![Got it title correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_title_correct.png)      |       Incorrect![Got it title incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_title_incorrect.png)      |

#### Implementation

Kotlin:

```KOTLIN
GotItTooltip(TOOLTIP_ID, GET_IT_TEXT, parentDisposable)
    .withHeader("The reader mode is on")
```

Java:

```JAVA
new GotItTooltip(TOOLTIP_ID, GET_IT_TEXT, parentDisposable)
    .withHeader("The reader mode is on");
```

### Step counter

Use a step counter to number a sequence of related Got It tooltips.

![Got it steps](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_steps.png)

### Shortcut

Use a shortcut if the tooltip describes an action that has a shortcut.

![Got it shortcut](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_shortcut.png)
#### Implementation

Kotlin:

```KOTLIN
GotItTooltip(
    TOOLTIP_ID,
    { "You can rename usages ${shortcut("My.Action")}" },
    parentDisposable
)
```

Java:

```JAVA
new GotItTooltip(
    TOOLTIP_ID,
    gotItTextBuilder -> {
        String shortcut = gotItTextBuilder.shortcut("My.Action");
        return "You can rename usages " + shortcut;
    },
    parentDisposable
);
```

### Link

Add a link if users might want to revert changes in a feature or configure it.

Note:
Only one link can be added

![Got it link](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_link.png)
#### Implementation

Kotlin:

```KOTLIN
GotItTooltip(TOOLTIP_ID, TOOLTIP_TEXT, parentDisposable)
    .withLink("Disable for all files", this::actionMethodReference)
```

Java:

```JAVA
new GotItTooltip(TOOLTIP_ID, TOOLTIP_TEXT, parentDisposable)
    .withLink("Disable for all files", this::actionMethodReference);
```

Add an external link if there is a help source that can further explain the functionality.

![Got it link ext](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_link_ext.png)
#### Implementation

Kotlin:

```KOTLIN
GotItTooltip(TOOLTIP_ID, GOT_IT_TEXT, parentDisposable)
    .withBrowserLink("How to use", new URL("https://example.com"))
```

Java:

```JAVA
new GotItTooltip(TOOLTIP_ID, GOT_IT_TEXT, parentDisposable)
    .withBrowserLink("How to use", new URL("https://example.com"));
```

## When to use

### Small UI controls

Point to small and essential controls that can be overlooked in a dense interface.

### New feature

Introduce users to a feature improvement contextually when they start using it. Explain how it works and highlight its benefits.

|        Correct![Got it feature correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_feature_correct.png)      |       Incorrect![Got it feature incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_feature_incorrect.png)      |

### Changed behavior

Suggest a new pattern to a user's task that improves their workflow.

### Ambiguous behavior

Explain behavior that is not clear from the UI.

For example, when extracting a method, users can change only the method name in the blue box. The tooltip explains where to change the order of parameters in the parentheses and other properties of a method:

![Got it ambiguous](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_ambiguous.png)

## When not to use

### Presenting a new tool

Don't use the Got It tooltip as a marketing tool. It distracts users, especially during startup. Use marketing channels for this purpose.

### Nothing to point to

When there is nothing to point to in a dialog or a tool window, use a [banner](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/banner.html).

|        Correct![Got it banner correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_banner_correct.png)      |       Incorrect![Got it banner incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_banner_incorrect.png)      |

### Feedback from the interface

Don't use Got It tooltips to give users feedback from the interface. Use [notifications](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/balloon.html) instead.

|        Correct![Got it feedback correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_feedback_correct.png)      |       Incorrect![Got it feedback incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_feedback_incorrect.png)      |

### New option in a tree or list

For updates to frequently used menus, use a badge instead of a Got It tooltip to avoid disrupting the user's existing workflow.

|        Correct![Got it tree correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_tree_correct.png)      |       Incorrect![Got it tree incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_tree_incorrect.png)      |

## How to use

### Single use

Show a Got It tooltip only once. Never show it again after the user closes it

### Showing a group of tooltips

Show a sequence of tooltips only when users initiate it. Users can start a tooltip tour, for example, by pressing a respective button in the interface.

For example, Start Quick Tour initiates a tour of the new functionality:

![Got it initiate](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_initiate.png)

### Text length and formatting

* Show no more than 5 lines of body text. If the text does not fit, leave only the essential information and add a link to a help article. Make the help text [short and descriptive](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/writing-short.html).

* Use sentence case both for the header and body text, and follow the [punctuation rules](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/punctuation.html).

* Don't use style formatting. It makes the tooltip harder to read.

|        Correct![Got it content correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_content_correct.png)      |       Incorrect![Got it content incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_content_incorrect.png)      |

### Positioning

Don't cover the information the user is currently working with.

|        Correct![Got it position correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_position_correct.png)      |       Incorrect![Got it position incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_position_incorrect.png)      |

#### Implementation

See four predefined point providers in the [GotItTooltip](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-impl/src/com/intellij/ui/GotItTooltip.kt) class.

Kotlin:

```KOTLIN
GotItTooltip(TOOLTIP_ID, GOT_IT_TEXT, parentDisposable)
    .show(gutterComponent, GotItTooltip.TOP_MIDDLE)
```

Java:

```JAVA
new GotItTooltip(TOOLTIP_ID, GOT_IT_TEXT, parentDisposable)
    .show(gutterComponent, GotItTooltip.TOP_MIDDLE);
```

### Timeout for hiding

Consider adding a timeout if:

* The text is no longer than 10 words.

* The tooltip appears at the place at which the user is currently looking.

* There is no link in the tooltip.

For example, the Got It tooltip has a timeout because the text is short, the user has just started the Rename refactoring, and is very likely looking at this place:

![Got it short](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/got_it_short.png)
#### Implementation

Default timeout duration is 5 seconds. A custom duration can be set:

Kotlin:

```KOTLIN
GotItTooltip(TOOLTIP_ID, GOT_IT_TEXT, parentDisposable)
    .withTimeout(3000)
```

Java:

```JAVA
new GotItTooltip(TOOLTIP_ID, GOT_IT_TEXT, parentDisposable)
    .withTimeout(3000);
```

### Versioning

If a tooltip is triggered by an action or plugin installation, do not tie them to the current IDE version. In this case, users might miss a tooltip if they are using this functionality or plugin for the first time in the next IDE version.

## Built-in behavior

### Frequency

By default, a tooltip is shown only once per user.

### Closable

The tooltip disappears when:

* `Esc` is pressed

* User clicks any place outside the tooltip

* On a timeout

### Multiple Got It tooltips

If several tooltips appear at the same time, they are shown one by one.

### Text width

The tooltip width adjusts automatically to make the right margin 16 px. Text width is 280 px by default.



# Group Header

<tldr>
Implementation: [TitledSeparator](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/TitledSeparator.java)
</tldr>

A group header clearly labels a group of UI controls.

![01 group header](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/01_group_header.png)

## When to use

Follow the rules in [Groups of controls](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/groups-of-controls.html).

Do not use group headers when each group contains 3 controls and less. Separate with [vertical insets](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/layout.html#organize-with-insets) instead.

Incorrect

![6 03 group incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/6_03_group_incorrect.png)
Each group has less than 3 controls. Group headers only add noise in this case because control labels are enough to understand their purpose.

Correct

![6 03 group correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/6_03_group_correct.png)

## How to use

Use title capitalization for the label.

Make the label short, preferably no more than 4 words. Avoid generic words, such as "General" or "Options". See [Writing short and clear](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/writing-short.html).

If a group contains rarely used or advanced settings, use a collapsible group header and collapse it by default.

![02 collapsed header](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/02_collapsed_header.png)



# Input Field

<tldr>
Implementation: [JBTextField](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/components/JBTextField.java)
</tldr>

An input field allows users to enter or edit a text line using the keyboard.

![Input](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input.png)

## When to use

Use an input field if it’s not possible to enumerate the most likely values. Otherwise, use a [combo box](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/combo-box.html) or a [drop-down list](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/drop-down.html).

| Correct |Incorrect |
| ![Input when to correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_when_to_correct.png) |![Input when to incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_when_to_incorrect.png) |

## When not to use

### Previous input is saved

If the previous user input must be preserved, use a [combo box](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/combo-box.html).

![Combobox when to use 1](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/combobox_when_to_use_1.png)

### Large input

Use a [text area](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/text-area.html) for long or multi-line input.

![Input text area](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_text_area.png)

### Space is limited

If the place is constrained, use an expandable input field [ExpandableTextField](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/components/fields/ExpandableTextField.java).
For more details, see [Expand button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/built-in-button.html#expand-a-field).

![Input text input expand](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_text_input_expand.png)

### Many predefined values

If there are many predefined values (for example, code snippets, commit author), add completion to the input field [TextFieldWithCompletion](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-impl/src/com/intellij/util/textCompletion/TextFieldWithCompletion.java). Show the completion popup when the user starts typing.

![Input completion](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_completion.png)

### Built-in buttons

Use [built-in buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/built-in-button.html) to help the user enter data. For example, to browse the disk.

### Search

Use a [search field](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/search-field.html) to input a search query.

![Input search](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_search.png)

### Password

If input data is secured, replace it with dots via [JBPasswordField](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/components/JBPasswordField.java).

![Input password](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_password.png)

### Choosing a color

Use a color box to choose a color.

![Input colour box](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_colour_box.png)

## How to use

### Label

A label accompanies each input field and indicates the information type.

#### General rules

* Labels should be [short and descriptive](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/writing-short.html).

* Write the label as a noun and end it with a colon.

* Don't use labels to tell users what to do.

* Use [sentence-style capitalization](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/capitalization.html#sentence).

| Correct![Input label 1 correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_label_1_correct.png) |Incorrect![Input label 1 incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_label_1_incorrect.png) |

#### Label as a phrase

When writing a label as a phrase, don't use colon and ending punctuation.

| Correct![Input label 2 correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_label_2_correct.png) |Incorrect![Input label 2 incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_label_2_incorrect.png) |

#### Grouped input fields

If there are several input fields in a form, make labels approximately the same length to avoid gaps between labels and fields.

| Correct![Input label 3 correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_label_3_correct.png) |Incorrect![Input label 3 incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_label_3_incorrect.png) |

#### Disabled state

If an input field is disabled, disable the label too.

![Input disabled](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_disabled.png)

#### Selectable label

Make the label text selectable. The user may want to search for this option on the Internet or to send a question to support.

![Input label selected](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_label_selected.png)

#### Positioning a label

Place the label on the left or above the input field. For more details, see the [Layout](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/layout.html) topic.

| Correct![Input positioning label 1](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_positioning_label_1.png) |Correct![Input positioning label 2](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_positioning_label_2.png) |

### Placeholder

Placeholder is gray text placed inside an input field. To show placeholder text, use `JBTextField.getEmptyText().setText(...)`.

#### General rules

* Use sentence-style capitalization.

* Don't use ending punctuation or ellipsis.

* Hide the placeholder when the user starts typing, not when the input field gets the focus.

#### Optional input field

Use the placeholder to indicate that an input field is optional.

![Input placeholder optional](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_placeholder_optional.png)

#### Default values

Use the placeholder to show the default value.

![Input placeholder default](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_placeholder_default.png)
If the user overwrites the value, it can be restored by removing the new value from the input field or by clicking the Reset to default link on the right.

![Input placeholder default reset](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_placeholder_default_reset.png)

#### Showing examples

Don't use the placeholder to show examples because the user can get the impression that the field is already filled. Provide examples or explanation under the input field (see [Context help](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/context-help.html)):

| Correct![Input placeholder example correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_placeholder_example_correct.png) |Incorrect![Input placeholder example incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_placeholder_example_incorrect.png) |

#### Don't use placeholders as labels

Don't use the placeholder as the field label. After the field has been filled, it is difficult to understand its purpose.

| Correct![Input placeholder label correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_placeholder_label_correct.png) |Incorrect![Input placeholder label incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_placeholder_label_incorrect.png) |

### Prefilled value

Pre-fill the field if it has the default or a frequently used value. Use the default text color for pre-filled values:

![Input prefilled](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_prefilled.png)
Note:
When naming a default entity like `scope` or `notebook` which can have multiple entities in a group, pre-fill it using the entity name with a sequential number: `scope-1`, `scope-2`, etc.

Don't use Unnamed as a prefilled value. It takes time to read it and does not help the user to fill the form.

| Correct![Input prefilled unnamed correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_prefilled_unnamed_correct.png) |Incorrect![Input prefilled unnamed incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_prefilled_unnamed_incorrect.png) |

### Field focus

When an input field gets the focus, place the caret at the end of the text:

![Input focus](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_focus.png)
If users are more likely to re-enter the entire value, select the whole text when the field gets the focus:

![Input focus selection](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_focus_selection.png)

### Validation

If the user enters an invalid value, highlight the field with red and show an error message in a tooltip. For more details, see [Validation errors](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/validation-errors.html).

![Input validation](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_validation.png)

## Sizes and placement

### Width

Choose the width appropriate for the most common values, but not less than 65px. The field width helps the user understand what value is expected and to make sure that they fill the field correctly.

| Correct![Input width 1 correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_width_1_correct.png) |Incorrect![Input width 1 incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_width_1_incorrect.png) |

If the input value is longer than the field width, show the beginning of the value when the field becomes inactive.

![Input width 2](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/input_width_2.png)

### How to layout

Follow the [labeled input controls](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/layout.html#labeled-input-controls).



# Link

<tldr>
Implementation: [ActionLink](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/components/ActionLink.kt), [DropDownLink](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/components/DropDownLink.kt)
</tldr>

![A preview of link types: default, drop-down, and external.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link.png)

## When to use

### Navigation inside a window

Use a regular link for navigation between pages of the same window. In the example below Manage scopes… opens another page in Settings for editing the values.

|          Correct         ![A vertical list of three options: 'Non-Project Files', 'Problems', and 'Production', followed by a 'Manage scopes…' link below.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_when_to_1_correct.png)      |         Incorrect         ![A vertical list of three options: 'Non-Project Files', 'Problems', and 'Production', followed 'Manage scopes' button below.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_when_to_1_incorrect.png)      |

### Web resources

Use an external link for navigation to web resources. See below for the [external link icon](#external-link-icon).

![Text 'Learn more about what is logged' with 'what is logged' as an external link with an arrow icon.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_when_to_2.png)

### Secondary actions in packed UI areas

Use a regular or [drop-down link](#drop-down-link) for secondary actions in packed or small UI areas.

![Build and run section with 'Modify options' drop-down link. Contains a Java SDK selector, a command line arguments selector, and a program arguments input.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_when_to_4.png)

### Secondary actions in a tree or table

#### Some items can be changed

Use a link as a secondary action for some items of a tree or table.

![A tree with a checkbox and four dependent controls, and links 'Set…' in the first and the fourth control](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_when_to_5.png)

#### All items can be changed

If a link in every tree or table line has meaningful formatting, leave it.

For example, links in the Push Commits window help understand the relation between them: [remote repository] : [branch]; moving these links elsewhere would break this meaning.

![Links in the Push Commits window 'origin : master'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_when_to_6_3.png)

## When not to use

### Primary actions

Use a [button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/button.html) or a [drop down list](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/drop-down.html) for primary actions. These controls can be selected from the keyboard and are bigger and easier to click.

|          Correct         ![The Commit Message input with primary and secondary actions as buttons.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_when_not_to_1_correct.png)      |         Incorrect         ![The Commit Message input with primary and secondary actions as links.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_when_not_to_1_incorrect.png)      |

### Secondary actions in a tree or table

#### Editable items

When all items can be changed, add an [icon button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/icon-button.html) to a toolbar.

|          Correct         ![Table with a toolbar with icon-buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_when_to_6_correct.png)      |         Incorrect         ![Table with a link 'Edit…' in every row](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_when_to_6_incorrect.png)      |

#### List of choices

For a list of choices, add a separate table column of drop-down cells (see [Table](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/table.html#editing-values)).

|          Correct         ![Table with a toolbar with icon-buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_when_not_to_3_correct.png)      |         Incorrect         ![Table with a link 'Edit…' in every row](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_when_not_to_3_incorrect.png)      |

### Simple UI

Use a [button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/button.html) or a [drop down list](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/drop-down.html) when a UI is not constrained.
These controls can be selected from the keyboard and are bigger and easier to click.

|        Correct       ![A stack of controls with a button 'Edit' following one of the controls.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_when_not_to_2_correct.png)      |
|        Incorrect       ![A stack of controls with a link 'Edit' following one of the controls.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_when_not_to_2_incorrect.png)      |

## How to use

### Writing guidelines

#### Use sentence capitalization

Follow the [sentence capitalization](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/capitalization.html#sentence) guideline.

|        Correct       ![A 'Modify options' drop-down with the sentence style capitalization.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_how_to_1_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![A 'Modify Options' drop-down with the title style capitalization.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_how_to_1_incorrect.png)      |

#### Ellipsis

Add an ellipsis to a link if it opens another UI area where input is possible. See examples for the [Button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/button.html).

|        Correct       ![A vertical list of three options: 'Non-Project Files', 'Problems', and 'Production', followed by a 'Manage scopes…' link below. The link has an ellipsis in the end.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_how_to_2_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Vertical list of three options: 'Non-Project Files', 'Problems', and 'Production', followed by a 'Manage scopes' link below. The link doesn't have an ellipsis in the end.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_how_to_2_incorrect.png)      |

#### Wording

Do not use words like `navigate` or `click here`. A link already implies navigation or clicking.

|        Correct       ![Link 'Proxy settings…'.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_how_to_3_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Link 'Navigate to general proxy settings'.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_how_to_3_incorrect.png)      |

|        Correct       ![Link 'Download drivers…'.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_how_to_4_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Text reading 'Click here to download drivers' where 'here' is a link.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_how_to_4_incorrect.png)      |

#### Make it informative

When possible, replace `Learn more` and other generic phrases with more informative ones.

|        Correct       ![Link 'How to use Closure Linter'.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_how_to_5_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Link 'Learn more'.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_how_to_5_incorrect.png)      |

### Link as a part of text

A link can be a part of a checkbox or radio button label or of any stand-alone text, like the text in an [empty state](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/empty-state.html) or in [context help](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/context-help.html):

![Checkbox 'Use console font instead of the default font' where 'default font' is a link.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_how_to_6.png)
Make a link the minimum phrase that is enough to understand what will happen without reading the whole text:

|        Correct       ![Text reading 'Learn more about what is logged' where 'what is logged' is a link.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_how_to_7_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Link 'Learn more about what is logged'.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_how_to_7_incorrect.png)      |

### External link icon

Add the arrow icon for an external link. The icon shows that the user will switch to a browser and lose the current context.

![Text 'Learn more about what is logged' where 'what is logged' is an external link with the external link icon.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_how_to_8.png)
#### Implementation

Kotlin:

```KOTLIN
val externalLink = ActionLink("External link") {
  BrowserUtil.browse("https://www.jetbrains.com")
}.apply {
  setExternalLinkIcon()
}
```

Java:

```JAVA
ActionLink externalLink = new ActionLink(
    "External link",
    event -> BrowserUtil.browse("https://www.jetbrains.com")
);
externalLink.setExternalLinkIcon();
```

### Help icon

Use the help icon in links in [empty states](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/empty-state.html) to indicate that this is an external help resource. The arrow icon in this case is unnecessary.

|        Correct       ![Empty state in the Database tool window with an explanation text and a help source link 'Defining a database' with the help icon.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_how_to_9_correct.png)      |       Incorrect       ![Empty state in the Database tool window with an explanation text and an external link 'Defining a database' with the external link icon.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_how_to_9_incorrect.png)      |

### Drop-down link

Drop-down links show a context menu or a popup. To implement, use [DropDownLink](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/components/DropDownLink.kt).

![Control 'Changes from 2 commits' where '2 commits' is a drop-down link opening a list of all commits](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/link_dropdown.png)

## Placement

* For default links follow [layout of buttons and links](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/layout.html#buttons-and-links).

* For drop-down links follow [layout of labeled controls](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/layout.html#labeled-input-controls).

## Built-in behavior

A focused link is activated from the keyboard with `Space`.



# Notifications

Notifications inform users about the status of user or system initiated operations. They can have different actions depending on the message.

Types of notifications:

* Alert

* [Banner](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/banner.html)

* [Notification balloon](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/balloon.html)

## What notification to use

Choose a notification type based on a combination of two factors:

1. Is user action required to proceed?

* [Required immediately](#action-is-required-immediately)

* [Required but not immediately](#action-is-required-but-not-immediately)

* [Not required](#action-is-not-required-to-proceed)

2. From what context the notification was initiated?

* Editor

* Tool window

* Dialog

* Any other location

### Action is required immediately

Use an alert in any context:
![An alert 'Open Project' asking where to open 'myJavaProject' with options to cancel, open in a new window or this window](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_type_alert.png)

### Action is required but not immediately

Use a [banner](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/banner.html) if the context is the editor, a tool window, or a dialog:
![A banner in the editor with a warning 'Project JDK is not defined' and action 'Setup JDK'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_type_banner_action_required_editor.png)

In any other context, use a [notification balloon](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/balloon.html).

### Action is not required to proceed

Use a [notification balloon](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/balloon.html) in any context except dialogs:
![A notification balloon warning about a shortcut conflict with a description and actions 'Modify shortcuts' and 'Don't show again'](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_type_balloon_action_not_required.png)

In a dialog, use a [banner](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/banner.html):
![A banner in a dialog with a notification 'Interactive lesson available' and actions 'Open lesson' and an icon button to close the banner](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_type_banner_action_required_dialog.png)



# Notification Balloon

<tldr>
Implementation: [Notifications](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/ide-core/src/com/intellij/notification/Notifications.java)

Related: [Notification Balloons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/notification-balloons.html)
</tldr>

Notification balloons inform users of the events or system states related to a project or IDE.

![A notification balloon for a found database connection with an action to connect to it](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon.png)

## Suggestion and timeline notifications

There are two types of notification balloons:

* Suggestion notifications show the recommended action as a noticeable button. Use to suggest an automatic configuration for a project or an IDE, or to ask for user input.

* Timeline notifications show useful actions as links. Use for showing results of long processes, automatic configuration, or actions without context.

These types appear in different sections of the Notifications tool window:

![The Notifications toolwindow with suggestion and timeline notifications in different sections](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon_toolwindow.png)

## When to use

### Show result of a potentially long process

Use a timeline notification.

![Two notifications with results of long processes: project build and git push](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon_timeline_long_process.png)

### Show result of an action without context

Use a timeline notification when an action was called from a context that is already closed, like a dialog or a popup.

![Two notifications with results of actions that are not tied to a particular dialog: the UI language was changed and project folders excluded from Windows Defender](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon_timeline_no_context_action.png)

### Show result of an automatic configuration

Use a timeline notification when the project or IDE settings were automatically configured, and the user might need to check the changes.

![A notification about automatic project configuration: the workspace is restored after a branch is checked out](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon_timeline_automatic_configuration.png)

### Suggest an action to configure a project or an IDE

Use a suggestion notification to promote an action for project or IDE configuration when not taking this action might lead to less optimal functioning or errors.

![Two examples of a suggestion notification for project or IDE configuration: Windows Defender affecting the IDE with a suggestion to explude a project from it, and a suggestion for switching the UI to an available language](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon_suggestion_configuration.png)

### Request user input

Use a suggestion notification to ask the user for an additional input or action that is not connected to their own workflows.

![Two suggestion notifications for requiring user input: a request to fill a survey and a notice about a discount for PhpStorm](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon_suggestion_request_input.png)

## How to use

### Sticky or timed

Sticky notifications stay on screen until the user clicks any of its actions or closes it. By default, use this behavior for [suggestion notifications](#suggestion-and-timeline-notifications).

Timed notifications stay on screen for 10 seconds and then hide. By default, use this behavior for [timeline notifications](#suggestion-and-timeline-notifications).

Change the default behavior if it makes sense in a particular use case.

### Message severity

#### Error

Use to inform of a critical event or state that might disrupt the user experience.

![An error notification about a plugin being suspended because it requires another plugin that is missing](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon_severity_error.png)

#### Warning

Use in case an event or state might slow down the user's work or require an action to fix the project or IDE settings.

![A warning notification about IDE shortcuts conflicting with macOS shortcuts](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon_severity_warning.png)

#### Information

Use in all other cases.

![An information notification requesting to fill a survey about a plugin](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon_severity_info.png)

When possible, use a plugin or functionality icon instead of the Info icon. This helps identifing the source of the notification quicker.

![Two notifications with dedicated icons instead of the generic info icon: database connection found with the database icon and suggested plugins found with the generic plugin icon](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon_plugin_icon.png)

### Text

#### Writing

[Write short and clear](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/writing-short.html) as notifications have limited space and may appear for a short time.

Use sentence case for both the title and the body.

Follow the [punctuation rules](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/punctuation.html).

#### Title

Describe the event and the context in which it occurred. The context could be the name of a plugin, library, or functionality.

#### Body

Provide the details on the event or system state to help users decide what to do next. Consider answering these questions:

* What was the cause of this state?

* What are the consequences?

* What is affected: files, libraries, versions, plugins, etc.?

#### Using only title or body

Use only the title when it is short and fits in one line.

![A notification with the title only about the number of files updated after git pull](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon_title_only.png)
Use only the body text when it fits in two lines and the title would duplicate its meaning.

Correct

![A notification with the body only about the workspace being restored after branch checkout](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon_body_only_correct.png)
Incorrect

![The same notification as above but with duplicating information in the title](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon_body_only_incorrect.png)

#### Long messages are collapsed

Only the first two lines of the body text are visible by default, the rest is shown when expanded. Place the most important information in the beginning of the body text so it is visible by default.

![A notification about Windows Defender slowing down the IDE in the collapsed and expanded states. The notification body is long and takes 9 lines](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon_body_two_lines.png)

### Actions

Add actions to help users take the next steps: fix a problem, view relevant information, configure settings, etc.

#### Number of actions

The preferable number of actions is two, as it is easier for the user to choose. If more than two actions are useful, place the most likely to be used first, and hide the others under the More dropdown:

![The Windows Defender notification with the primary action "Exclude folders" on the left and 3 more actions under the "More" dropdown link](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon_more_actions.png)

#### Actions in error and warning notifications

If the notification reports an error or warning, always provide an action to help users fix the problem:

![An error notification about the plugin being suspended because it requires another plugin to work with actions "Manage plugins" and "Disable the suspended plugin"](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon_error_actions.png)
If no actions are available, provide more details in the body text: how to fix or what was the cause.

Correct

![A notification about a plugin being incompatible with the current IDE version with a suggestion to update the plugin](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon_error_actions_text_correct.png)
Incorrect

![The name notification but without the suggestion to update the plugin](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon_error_actions_text_incorrect.png)

#### The "Don't show again" action

If the notification is informational, and there is a possibility it might appear too often, add the Don’t show again action:

![A notification about a database connection found with the "Don't show again link"](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/notification_balloon.png)

#### Capitalization

Use sentence capitalization for all actions in notification balloons.

## Naming a notification group

Each notification balloon belongs to a group. Groups can be seen in `Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Notifications`.

To name a notification group, follow these rules:

* Name the group with an ending to the phrase "Notifications in this group notify the user about…". Examples: Automatic indent detection, Content root duplicates.

* If a name about a particular process or event cannot be given, use the name of a subsystem or plugin. Examples: HTTP Client, Power Save Mode.

* When a group contains notifications about errors or problems, do not use a verb. Example: Debugger errors, not Debugger errors found.

* Do not use words "notification" or "group". They are implied from the settings context.



# Banner

<tldr>
Implementation: [EditorNotificationProvider](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/EditorNotificationProvider.java)

Related: [Editor Banner](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/informing-users.html#editor-banner)
</tldr>

A banner notification informs the user about the state of a specific context in the project. For example, when there is a missing or broken configuration for some file.

![Banner error](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/banner_error.png)

## When to use

Use a banner if user actions should attract attention in a file tab, tool window, or dialog, but are not required immediately.

![Tool window](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tool-window.png)
Reconnecting to the database is required to make edits.

![Dialog example](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/dialog-example.png)
The component needs to be installed to run the available virtual devices.

Do not use a banner if there is no particular UI component it can be tied to. Use a [balloon notification](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/balloon.html) in the main window instead.

For all other cases, choose another notification type.

### Types of banners

#### Information

Use when actions can improve the user’s workflow but are considered optional and can be safely ignored.

![Information example](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/information-example.png)
The new tool window UI is suggested to improve the workflow for version control.

#### Warning

Use to suggest actions that can impact the user’s workflow.

![Warning example](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/warning-example.png)
Generated files should be edited directly.

#### Error

Use to suggest actions that are required to unblock the user’s workflow.

![Banner error](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/banner_error.png)
Syntax highlighting and other inspections are broken until a JDK is defined for the project.

## How to use

![Banner structure](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/banner_structure.png)
### Message

* The message should be [short and descriptive](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/writing-short.html) (two sentences at most) and follow the [Punctuation](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/punctuation.html) guide.

* Use sentence case capitalization.

### Actions

* The action name should be [short and descriptive](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/writing-short.html), preferably not longer than two–three words.

* Use sentence case capitalization.

* Limit the number of actions to two to make the call to action clear in the specific context.

* Use the built-in 'Hide' action instead of creating a separate one.

### Icon (optional)

* 16×16 icons can be used to complement the message, e.g., a gift icon to advertise functionality.

### Placement

* Place the banner at the top of the related UI component.

* It can float or be adjacent to the content, depending on the amount of available space and whether the content’s vertical shifting needs to be minimized.

![Float example](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/float-example.png)
The banner floats on top of the preview surface to reduce shifting during code editing.



# Progress Indicators

<tldr>
Implementation: Progress tracking in [Progress API](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/background-processes.html#tracking-progress) and [Kotlin Coroutines](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/execution-contexts.html#progress-reporting)
</tldr>

Progress indicators inform users about an ongoing operation. There are three types of indicators:

* [Loader](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/loader.html)

* [Progress text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/progress-text.html)

* [Progress bar](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/progress-bar.html)

## Which indicator to use

If an operation lasts for less than a second in most cases, do not show any progress indicator. Progress indicators for a short operation are distracting.

If the user has to wait until a process completes to continue working with the app, show a progress bar in a modal dialog.

![Progress dialog](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/progress_dialog.png)
If the progress is non-modal, select progress indicator based on where it appears.

* [Input field, combo box, drop-down](#input-field-combo-box-drop-down)

* [Search field](#search-field)

* [Tree, list, tool window](#tree-list-tool-window)

* [Breadcrumb and dialog label](#breadcrumb-and-dialog-label)

* [Settings dialog](#settings-dialog)

* [Empty state](#empty-state)

* [Main window](#main-window)

### Input field, combo box, drop-down

Place the loader inside an input field on the right to show that the field content is being loaded or checked.

![Combo box loader](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/combo_box_loader.png)

### Search field

Place the loader on the right to show that search is being performed.

![Search field loader](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field_loader.png)

### Tree, list, tool window

If each tree node loads independently, and it’s important to know the current state of each node, show the loader instead of the node icon:

![Tree loader icon](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tree_loader_icon.png)
If nodes do not have icons, or icons can’t be replaced for some reason, show progress text after the node’s label:

![Tree text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tree_text.png)
If the loader applies to the whole content, place it in the top right corner:

![Tree loader corner](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tree_loader_corner.png)
If processes start simultaneously and have the same execution time, place the loader in the top right corner of the area.
For example, in the Push dialog, repositories are loaded at the same time.
Loaders in each line will blink at the same time and will look distracting.

![Tree loader push](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tree_loader_push.png)
If the top right corner of the area is taken with content and there is no space for the loader, show the progress bar at the top of the tool window.
For example, the VCS Log tool window has a progress bar at the top when the content is loading or during searching.

![Progress tool window](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/progress_tool_window.png)

### Breadcrumb and dialog label

Place the loader after breadcrumbs or a dialog label to show that the page is being loaded:

![Breadcrumb loader](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/breadcrumb_loader.png)

### Settings dialog

If some settings or configurations take a significant time to load, it’s preferable to reserve space for a progress bar.
For example, show a progress bar while installing a plugin:

![Settings loader](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/settings_loader.png)

### Empty state

If the state is empty, show progress text. For example, in search dialogs, and the details panel in settings or tool windows:

![Empty state text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_text.png)
Show one more progress indicator, e.g., a loader like on the example above, if loading continues when some data is already displayed.

If a process takes longer than 4 seconds, provide [process details](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/progress-text.html#details), e.g., the time left or passed, work units
like the current step, to indicate that the process is being performed and is not hanging:

![Empty state details](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_details.png)
If it’s not possible to provide progress details, show the loader to indicate that a long process is not frozen:

![Empty state loader](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_loader.png)

### Main window

If a process is long and can run in the background, show the progress bar in the main window in the status bar:

![Status bar progress](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/status_bar_progress.png)
Or in a non-modal dialog:

![Tasks dialog](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/tasks_dialog.png)



# Loader

<tldr>
Implementation: [AnimatedIcon.Default](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/ide-core/src/com/intellij/ui/AnimatedIcon.java)

Related: [Animated Icons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/icons.html#animated-icons)
</tldr>

A loader informs users about performing a lengthy operation.

![Loader](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/loader.png)

## When to use

Follow the rules for [progress indicators](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/progress-indicators.html).

## How to use

The loader form and sizes are the same in all themes. Use the default 16×16 loader in all cases.

Kotlin:

```KOTLIN
JLabel(
    "Loading...",
    AnimatedIcon.Default(),
    SwingConstants.LEFT
)
```

Java:

```JAVA
new JLabel(
    "Loading...",
    new AnimatedIcon.Default(),
    SwingConstants.LEFT
);
```

A loader may have a label if the process is long and the loader is shown in an empty area. In this case, use a [progress text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/progress-text.html) as the label:

![Loader with progress text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/loader_with_progress_text.png)
Remove the loader as soon as the process completes.

## Placement

|  Inside a field  | ![Placement field](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/placement_field.png)  |
|           ```JAVA ExpandableTextField textField = new ExpandableTextField(); textField.addExtension(   Extension.create(new AnimatedIcon.Default(), null, null) ); ```        |
| In a corner | ![Placement corner](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/placement_corner.png)      |
|   Next to an item  | ![Placement item](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/placement_item.png)  |
|  Before a progress text  | ![Placement progress text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/placement_progress_text.png)      |



# Progress Bar

<tldr>
Implementation: [JProgressBar](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/uiswing/components/progress.html)
</tldr>

A progress bar informs users about the progress of a lengthy operation.

![01 progress bar](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/01%20progress_bar.png)

## When to use

Follow the rules for [progress indicators](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/progress-indicators.html).

## How to use

### Types

Use a determinate progress bar if the process duration is known. Otherwise, use indeterminate progress bar:

![02 determinate and indeterminate](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/02%20determinate_and_%20indeterminate.png)
If an indeterminate process reaches a point where its duration can be determined, switch to a determinate progress bar:

![04 determinate to indeterminate](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/04%20determinate_to_indeterminate.png)

### Process name and details

A progress bar can have a process name and process details.

#### Process name

Show the name of the operation being performed above the progress bar:

![05 process name](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/05_process%20name.png)
If the vertical space is limited, place the process name with a colon on the left:

![07 process name on the left](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/07%20process_name_on_the_left.png)

#### Process details

Show information about the current stage of an operation to make long-running tasks more predictable and manageable.

Show details below the progress bar on a single line. The length of details is limited by the width of the progress bar.

![05 process details](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/05_process%20details.png)
For wording, follow the rules for [progress text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/progress-text.html).

Examples:

* The current step: "Uploading file 3 of 10"

* The name of a file, module, or library: "Fetching guava-31.1.jar"

* Remaining time or percentage completed

### Process controls

Place process controls on the right next to the progress bar. On hover over the icon, show the name of the control under the progress bar instead of process details.

![17 stop button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/17%20stop_button.png)
#### Cancel or Stop button

Add a Cancel button if the process can be safely interrupted. If interrupting the process does not restore the system to its previous state, name the button Stop.

![17 cancel button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/17%20cancel_button.png)

#### Pause button

If the process takes a long time and can prevent the user from performing tasks, provide an option to pause a process.

Note:

It is recommended to run the process in the background so it doesn’t interrupt the user, instead of offering a pause option.

|        ![Pause button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/18%20pause_button.png)      |       Replace process details with the "Pause" comment on hover over the Pause icon.        |
|           ![Process on pause](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/19%20resume_button.png)          |         If a user pauses the process, show "Paused" under the progress bar. Replace the Pause icon with Resume.         |
|           ![Resume button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/20%20resume_button.png)          |         Show "Resume" under the progress bar and when hovered over the Resume button.         |

### Placement

If you need to use the progress bar among other controls, place it close to the control that starts the process.

![23 placement](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/23%20placement.png)
#### In dialog or popup

Note:

Place the progress bar in a modal dialog if the IDE cannot function properly until  the process is completed.

Use a process name as a dialog or popup header, capitalize the title and remove the ellipsis. Process details appear above the progress bar.
For a single progress bar, use a button to cancel or pause the process instead of an icon:

![13 in dialog](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/13%20in_dialog.png)
For several processes in a group, add a common header and use icons for process controls:

![16 process control](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/16%20process_control.png)

#### Inline progress

Use inline progress to indicate that content is being updated. The user can continue working with the content, but should see that a background process is in progress.

Do not show a process name for an inline progress.

![09 inline processes](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/09%20inline_processes.png)

#### Process status

If a process consists of substeps that can fail but do not terminate the process, then use green and red colors to show the intermediate status.
For example, show the status of the running tests:

![15 process status](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/15%20process_status.png)

#### Process complition

Hide the progress bar as soon as the process completes.



# Progress Text

![Desc](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/desc.png)

## When to use

Follow the rules for [progress indicators](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/progress-indicators.html).

## How to use

### Process name

Use the progressive form of the verb which describes the process, for example:

![Progressive form](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/progressive_form.png)
Add an ellipsis at the end to show that an action is in progress.

Use sentence case for process names.

A process name remains unchanged while the process runs.

Do not animate the ellipsis, as it attracts too much attention.
The progressive verb form, the text position and the style are enough to understand that this is an action in progress.

### Details

Use sentence case for details.

Do not provide details that are meaningless for the user, for example, "Please wait":

Incorrect

![Meaningless](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/meaningless.png)
Add time units if the remaining time can be predicted.

Round up the first time unit to one of the following numeric anchors: 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 15, 20 and 30.
For example, if there are 7 minutes and 50 seconds remaining, the progress text should read "About 10 minutes left".
If less than 5 seconds are left, it should say "About 5 seconds left".

![Time](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/time.png)
Use work units if the remaining time cannot be predicted, as they help the user understand why the process takes so long.

Work units: the current step, the currently processed file, the number of processed files/tde amount of information, the percentage of work completed, and so on:

![Work](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/work.png)
The time passed if the user controls the process, for example, needs to stop it after a certain time:

![Passed](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/passed.png)
Update the timer every second.

### Cancellation action

If the process can be cancelled, add a [link](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/link.html) for the cancel action for an empty state:

![Cancellation](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/cancellation.png)
Use title case for the cancel action.

Replace progress text with the loaded data or an [empty state](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/empty-state.html) when the process has finished.
Show another progress indicator, e.g., a loader as in the example below, if loading continues after some data has been displayed.

![Empty state text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty_state_text.png)

### Trees
