Do not show details or a link to cancel the operation for progress in trees and lists. Only show the process name since space is limited here.

## Sizes and placement

### Empty state

Center-align the first line of the progress text if it is no longer than 200px.
If it is longer than 200px, center-align characters from the first 200px and put the rest of the characters to the right.

Left-align subsequent lines with the first line.

The minimum text width is 40 characters.
If an area is too narrow to fit the minimum text width, show text using the whole width, including margins.
If no space is left, hide the text under area borders.

Wrap text when the area’s width changes.

Fields and vertical spaces:

![Fields](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/fields.png)

### Tree

![Progress text tree](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/progress_text_tree.png)

## Style

Font color is the same as for [Empty state](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/empty-state.html) text.



# Radio Button

<tldr>
Implementation: [JBRadioButton](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/components/JBRadioButton.java)
</tldr>

![01 radio button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/01_Radio%20Button.png)

## When to use

Use a radio button group to choose one option from 2 to 4 mutually exclusive options.

## When not to use

### Several options can be selected

Use a group of [checkboxes](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/checkbox.html) when several options can be selected.

### Yes or No Options

For only two opposing yes/no options, use a checkbox.

|        Correct![A correct example of using a checkbox instead of radiobuttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/02_When_to_use_correct.png)      |       Incorrect![An incorrect example of using radiobuttons instead of a checkbox](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/02_When_to_use_incorrect.png)      |

### 2-5 options with short labels

If the options have short labels, use a segmented button.

![03 when to use segmented button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/03_When_to_use_Segmented_button.png)

### When to use a drop-down instead

Consider using a [drop-down list](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/drop-down.html) if:

* There are more than 5 options:

|        Correct![A correct example of using a drop-down list instead of radiobuttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/04_When_to_use_correct.png)      |       Incorrect![An incorrect example of using radiobuttons for a list of 5 or more options](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/04_When_to_use_incorrect.png)      |

* The options have long labels.

* The screen space is limited.

* The option might be used less often than other options on the screen.

* There are other drop-down lists in the same group of UI components. A radio button group is more noticeable than a drop-down list, so it will look like a more important setting.

* The setting combines several UI components into one control:

![05 when to use segmented button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/05_When_to_use_Segmented_button.png)

## How to use

### Label

| ![Label example](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/06_How_to_use.png) |A label accompanies each radio button and is placed next to it.   |
| ![An example of a label spanning two lines.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/07_How_to_use.png) |If a label is long, split it into two lines. Avoid labels that take more than two lines. See recommendations on writing concise labels below.   |

#### Implementation

Kotlin UI DSL:

```KOTLIN
radioButton(
    "<html>Show options before adding<br>to version control</html>")
```

Java:

```JAVA
new JRadioButton(
    "<html>Show options before adding<br>to version control</html>");
```

### Writing guidelines

* Use sentence-style capitalization.

* Do not use ending punctuation.

* Use the imperative form of verbs.

* Do not use negation in labels as it complicates understanding.

* Make labels short and intelligible — see [Writing short and clear text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/writing-short.html).

|        Correct![A correct example of using a drop-down list instead of radiobuttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/08_How_to_use_correct.png)      |       Incorrect![An incorrect example of using radiobuttons for a list of 5 or more options](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/08_How_to_use_incorrect.png)      |

### Group label

| ![Label example](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/10_How_to_use.png) |Always start a radio button group with a group label to explain what the options are for. Use a colon at the end of a group label.   |
| ![An example of a label spanning two lines.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/09_How_to_use.png) |Use a checkbox or another radio button as a group label if the radio button group needs to be turned on or off.   |

## Sizes and placement

Follow the layout of [checkboxes and radio-buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/layout.html#checkboxes-and-radio-buttons)



# Scrollbar

<tldr>
Implementation: [JBScrollBar](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/components/JBScrollBar.java)
</tldr>

The scrollbar allows users to browse content that’s larger than the visible area, such as text or images, by scrolling it horizontally or vertically.

![Scrollbar small](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/scrollbar-small.png)

## Parts of a scrollbar

A scroll bar consists of a track, a thumb, and a status icon if there is a known status for displayed content.

![Scrollbar detailed](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/scrollbar-detailed.png)
### Track

A track represents the overall length or width of the document.

The track can contain optional markers for quicker navigation between the important parts of the document, for example:

* The occurrences of a search string.

* Breakpoints and the current execution lines.

* A place where an inspection failed.

* Files with errors laid out in a tree.

* Changed parts of a file.

A marker can fit the track width or be placed to the left of the track. Use the latter when you expect the marked region to be tall.

Hovering over the track can also show a lens with a preview of the content at the corresponding position in the document.
This can be useful in large documents when it is not desirable to change the viewpoint:

![Lens temp](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/lens-temp.png)

### Thumb

A thumb represents the visible portion of the content. For example, a small thumb indicates that there’s lots of content available for scrolling.

### Status icon (optional)

A status icon shows the overall status of inspections performed on the content and allows you to avoid scrolling over the entire view.
If at least one inspection has failed, the overall status should be the status of that inspection.

![Commit](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/commit.png)

## How to use

Respect the OS settings when showing the scrollbar.
For example, on macOS you can hide the scrollbar until you scroll the content.
Always show the scrollbar when it is important to understand which part of the content is currently shown.
For example, the scrollbar in the Editor helps users understand the location of the current code fragment and the overall size of the currently opened file.

Show the track on hover to make the clickable area clearer. Consider not showing the track on hover if it might have more than 5–10 stripes at a time.

Increase the thumb contrast against the background on hover and when scrolling to make it more prominent.

Clicking the track above/below the thumb scrolls one page up/down the viewpoint.
This allows you to hide the up/down icons on the scrollbar to lessen the visual noise and to scroll with mouse-clicks.
Track markers serve as a mini-map of the document.
If they are present, clicking them takes you to the position that this marker is pointing to without having to scroll down the page.
Change the cursor to "Hand" when hovering such scrollbars.

When showing a text, wrap it instead of showing the horizontal scrollbar when possible. With both scrollbars, it is harder to manipulate the content.

Incorrect

![Soft wrap incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/soft-wrap-incorrect.png)
Correct

![Soft wrap correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/soft-wrap-correct.png)
A horizontal scroll bar can be added for code snippets or for formatted input. Use the context menu to enable soft-wrapping.

Correct

![Soft wrap context](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/soft-wrap-context.png)
Show only 1 scrollbar per table which scrolls the entire table:

Incorrect

![Table scrollbar incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/table-scrollbar-incorrect.png)
Correct

![Table scrollbar correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/table-scrollbar-correct.png)

## Placement

Reserve the space for a vertical scrollbar if there is a column on the right side, otherwise the scrollbar always overlaps content.

Incorrect

![Vertical scrollbar incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/vertical-scrollbar-incorrect.png)
Correct

![Vertical scrollbar correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/vertical-scrollbar-correct.png)

## Style

| Windows/Linux |macOS |
------------------------
| ![Win light](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/win-light.png) |![Mac light](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/mac-light.png) |



# Search Field

<tldr>
Implementation: [SearchTextField](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/SearchTextField.java)
</tldr>

A search field is an [input field](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/input-field.html) that helps users locate objects, actions, or text.

![Search field](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field.png)

## When to use

Use a search field when specific objects are difficult to find at a glance:

* There are many objects, as in the VCS Log table or in the Editor with a large file opened.

* Objects aren't in a single location, for example, controls are located on different setting pages.

## How to use

### Label

Don't add a label Search to the search field. The magnifying glass icon is self-explanatory.

| Correct![Search field label correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field_label_correct.png) |Incorrect![Search field label incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field_label_incorrect.png) |

### Placeholder

Provide hints such as search scope as placeholder text.

![Search field hints](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field_hints.png)

### Search and Replace fields

Mark the Search and Replace fields with placeholders when shown together to distinguish between them:

![Search field search replace](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field_search_replace.png)

### Search options

Use [icon buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/icon-button.html) inside the search field to save space and not to overload the UI.

![Search field search options](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field_search_options.png)
Icon buttons should change background color when enabled so that it is clear which options are currently enabled.

![Search field enabled icons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field_enabled_icons.png)

### Tab navigation

Make icon buttons easily accessible with Tab. Focused button should have a colored border.

![Search field tab focus](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field_tab_focus.png)

### Clear a search string

Show the Clear button ![](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field_close_icon.png) when the search field has been filled.
When the button is clicked, clear the search field and restore the content to its default state.

![Search field clear search](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field_clear_search.png)
When search can be configured with options, show the clear button on the left of the option buttons.
This way, option buttons won't jump when the clear button appears.

![Search field](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field.png)

### Multiline search strings

If multiline search is needed, use the New Line ![](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field_new_line_icon.png) action button. It should be placed on the left of the rest of the search options.

![Search field multiline](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field_multiline.png)
The default shortcut for the New Line action: `⇧⌘⏎` for macOS and `Ctrl + Shift + Enter` for Windows/Linux.

### Filters

Provide filters for complex searches. Don't use filter attributes in the search query.

| Correct![Search field attributes correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field_attributes_correct.png) |Incorrect![Search field attributes incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field_attributes_incorrect.png) |

### Search history

Use the magnifying glass icon with an arrow when search history is available. Show search history in a popup when clicking on the magnifying glass icon.

![Search field history](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field_history.png)
The keyboard shortcut for the History action is `Alt + Down` on all systems.

Add a search string to history:

* On `Enter` for searches that are executed.

* When the search field loses focus for searches that are executed on any keystroke.

## Sizes and placement

### Placement

Put the search field on top of the content that is being searched and align them vertically.
For example, the search field in Settings dialog is aligned with the filtered settings tree.

![Search field placement](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field_placement.png)
#### Speed Search

Show the search field on demand when search is supplementary to other functionality or if space is limited. The search field should be accessible with `⌘+F` on macOS and `Ctrl + F` on Windows/Linux.
For example, space in the Project view is limited and too loaded to always show the Search bar:

![Search field project](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search_field_project.png)

### Sizes

#### Grouped with other controls

For a search field which is displayed as an input field in a group of controls, for example, in a tool window toolbar, follow the [input sizes guideline](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/input-field.html#sizes-and-placement).

#### Above lists and trees

When placed above lists or trees, expand the field to the width of the list or tree.



# Table

<tldr>
Implementation: [JBTable](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/table/JBTable.java)
</tldr>

![Table table](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/table_table.png)

## When to use

Use tables so that users can review, enter or edit uniform sets of data or options. For example:

* `Git | Show Git Log`

* `Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Path Variables`

* `Settings | Appearance & Behavior | File Colors`

Use tables:

* To compare data in a set, for example, in the File Colors table, it is convenient to compare file colors with one another and make sure that they are distinguishable:

* ![File colors](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/fileColors.png)

* To search by all parameters in a data set, for example, in the File History table, it is possible to quickly filter the table by the date, author or commit message.

![Table history](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/table_history.png)
Do not use tables:

* For hierarchical structures. Use Tree View instead.

* When there are more than 4 options per entry. Use the Master-Detail layout instead.

* When at least one of the options requires a multi-line control, for example, the Text Area in `Settings | Editor | Copyright | Copyright Profiles`. Use Master-Detail layout instead: ![Master detail](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/master-detail.png)

## How to use

### Label

A label is optional for tables.

Add a label if the table content is not obvious from the dialog title or the table header. For example, in the table that lets you configure filters for import and completion per-scope:

![Table label](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/table_label.png)
Avoid a label if it duplicates the dialog title or the table header. For example, there is no need for a label in the `JavaScript | Libraries` table since the Settings page title and the table context make it clear what is in the table:

![Label header](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/label-header.png)
Add a label if the control above can be mistaken for a table header:

![Bytecode version](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/bytecode-version.png)
Do not add a label to explain the table behavior. Use context help instead:

Incorrect

![Label help header](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/label-help-header.png)
Correct

![Label help](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/label-help.png)
Follow the rules for the [Input field](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/input-field.html):

* The label should be short and descriptive.

* A label must be a noun phrase punctuated with a colon.

* Use sentence-style capitalization.

* If a table is disabled, disable the label.

* Make label text selectable.

Always put the label on top of the table.

Do not use a Group separator instead of a Table label. A horizontal line is redundant here:

Incorrect

![Label group incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/label-group-incorrect.png)
Correct

![Table label](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/table_label.png)

### Header

A table header is the row at the top of the table that helps identify the columns below each of the headers. Follow these rules:

Add a header to a table if table data is non-descriptive or ambiguous.
For example, in the Environment Variables table a header is required, since that content of each column is not clear:

Correct

![Header needed correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/header-needed-correct.png)
Incorrect

![Header needed incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/header-needed-incorrect.png)
Do not use a header if all columns in a table have self-descriptive content, for example, names, dates, color previews, etc. For example, a header in File History is redundant:

Correct

![Table history](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/table_history.png)
Incorrect

![History header redundant](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/history-header-redundant.png)
Labels in a header should be short and descriptive. Try to avoid headers which are too long for the content in the rows below. [How to write texts](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/writing-short.html).

Use nouns and noun phrases.

Use title-case capitalization.

Freeze a headers when scrolling the table. A header provides useful context and should not be hidden.

Align header with the content in the column below:

![File colors alignment](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/fileColorsAlignment.png)

### Placeholder

A table placeholder is shown when there is no data yet. Always put meaningful text here, do not write "Nothing to show".

![Empty incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty-incorrect.png)
It is better to add a reason why a table is empty, and an action link to fill it:

![Empty correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/empty-correct.png)
See more on empty tables [here](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/empty-state.html).

### Toolbar

Add a toolbar to provide actions which help manipulate data in the table (add, remove, import, etc.):

![Too long line](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/too-long-line.png)
Use the [ToolbarDecorator](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/ToolbarDecorator.java) class to implement such a toolbar. See more on toolbars [here](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/toolbar.html).

### Zebra striping and inner borders

Zebra striping is alternate highlighting of lines or rows in data tables or forms.

Use stripes if you want to help users distinguish between different data sets. For example, the current branch is highlighted differently from other branches:

![History zebra](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/history-zebra.png)
Do not use stripes In a simple data set as guides to track content between columns. Alternating backgrounds create two distinct layers of focus while the type of data in different rows is the same.

Incorrect

![Table zebra incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/table-zebra-incorrect.png)
Default line height, [proper column width](#sizes-and-placement) and highlighting rows on mouse hover should provide enough guidance to track content.
For example, look at the same table without stripes, with bigger line height and adjusted column width:

Correct

![Table table](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/table_table.png)
Bigger distance between groups of related information can also help in tracking content. Line height between groups should be increased by 4px for each group level.

For example, look at the File History table grouped by commit, author, and date:

![History grouped](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/history-grouped.png)
Do not add borders between rows or columns, they add unnecessary noise to the table:

Incorrect

![Inner borders incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inner-borders-incorrect.png)
Correct

![Inner borders](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inner-borders.png)

### Interaction

Highlight the hovered row to assist in tracking content across columns:

![Table hover](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/table_hover.png)
Change the background to active selection color for the selected row when the table is focused:

![Selection active](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/selection-active.png)
and to inactive selection when the focus is on another element:

![Selection inactive](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/selection-inactive.png)
Do not leave the active selection color in the table when the focus switches to some other element.
It is otherwise confusing which element is currently active.

Columns in tables should be resizable to allow users to set a comfortable column width.
Change the mouse cursor to "Horizontal Resize" when hovering the rectangular area between columns.
This area is defined by table height and by 2px padding around the columns’ divider.
This makes it clear that columns can be resized even in a table without a header:

![Resize](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/resize.png)
Double click when the "Horizontal Resize" cursor is activated, should auto resize the column to fit the content.

If column sorting is available, display the sorting state in the column header.
If the user clicks on a column that is already sorted, reverse the sorting order and rotate the sorting icon:

![Sorting](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/sorting.png)
Add sorting to a table if the default sorting by one column may be insufficient to scan the data set.
For example, in the table above, it is useful to be able to sort both by path and encoding to quickly find all paths with a specific encoding,
or to find a specific path in the sorted list.

If columns can be reordered, change the cursor to "Hand" when hovering the table header, and allow changing their order by dragging the table header.

In tables without a header show the drag icon on top of the column when hovering it:

![History drag](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/history-drag.png)
Change the cursor to "Hand" on the icon hover:

![History drag cursor](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/history-drag-cursor.png)
Allow dragging a column when the cursor is placed anyplace over this column.
This makes it clear that columns can be dragged even if there is no table header.

In disabled table greyed-out text, disable controls and any interaction:

![Table disabled](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/table_disabled.png)

### Editing values

If data in a cell is editable or configurable:

Allow in-place editing of content for text data. It should be possible to activate editing on mouse click:

![Inline edit](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline-edit.png)
The line with the edited cell should be selected.
The edited cell should have borders, and their color should be the same as the color for [Input field](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/input-field.html) borders.

Allow in-place editing for paths and add the Browse button to the cell:

![Inline edit path](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inline-edit-path.png)
Show a separate dialog for non-text data, for example, a color chooser for colors.

Do not show a separate dialog for editing simple data rows without a compound preview (an example of a compound preview can be found in `Settings | Editor | Language Injections`).
For example, there is no need for a separate dialog in the `Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Path Variables` table, as all editing could be done in place.

If it’s possible to enumerate less than 15 most likely or valid variants, show a combobox-like configurable with a down-arrow icon and a popup on click:

![Combo](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/combo.png)
Show the combo icon only on hover or when the corresponding line is selected. A lot of arrows in one column form their own information layers and attract too much attention.

If there are more than 15 variants, show a completion popup.

Do not use a full-size combobox inside tables. It looks inconsistent and has too many details for a table; a simple dropdown icon with the variants popup is enough.

Incorrect

![Combo incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/combo-incorrect.png)

## Sizes and placement

### Sizes

Choose a column width appropriate for the most common values, but no less than 65px. Too wide columns make it hard to read data.

Correct

![File colors](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/fileColors.png)
Incorrect

![File colors too wide](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/fileColorsTooWide.png)
The minimum table width is 350px. If a table is too narrow after you have adjusted column widths, add space to the rightmost column.

Add space to the rightmost column if you need to align it with other tables in the same window.

If content doesn't fit a cell's width, cut the text by the right border:

![Too long line](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/too-long-line.png)
Do not put ellipsis at the end of a cropped line, as it can be confused with the content.
Also, ellipsis can form a separate redundant column when content in the majority of cells in one column doesn't fit its width.

Do not add a fade-away gradient for cropped text, as it adds too many shades to a table text, and they attract too much attention.

### Placement

Do not put vertical elements (for example, diagrams) in the middle of a table, as they prevent users from scanning data easily:

Incorrect

![History graph incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/history-graph-incorrect.png)
Place them closer to the sides instead:

Correct

![Table history](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/table_history.png)
Right-align numbers when it is useful to compare them by their length. Left-align all the other content.

![Right align numbers](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/rightAlignNumbers.png)
For aligning in a dialog with other controls, see [Layout](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/layout.html).

## Style

| IntelliJ |![Table intellij](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/table_intellij.png) |
| Darcula |![Table darcula](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/table_darcula.png) |



# Tabs

<tldr>
Implementation: [JBTabbedPane](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/components/JBTabbedPane.java)
</tldr>

![Tabs](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/01_Tabs.png)

## When to use

Use tabs to organize related content. Follow rules for [Groups of controls](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/groups-of-controls.html).

Note:

For editor tabs, use another component — [JBEditorTabs](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/tabs/impl/JBEditorTabs.kt)

In tool windows, tabs are generated automatically. See [Tool window](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/tool-window.html).

## How to use

### Label

* Use title capitalization for tab labels.

* Make labels short, preferably no more than 3 words.

* Avoid generic words such as "General" or "Advanced".

* See [Writing short and clear](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/writing-short.html).

Correct

![Hiding tabs that do not fit](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/02_How_to_use_correct.png)
Incorrect

![Hiding tabs that do not fit](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/02_How_to_use_incorrect.png)

### Tab Order and Layout

Place the most frequently used content in the first tab.

Tabs that do not fit allotted screen space automatically hide under the dropdown component. It is better to add no more than 8 tabs, but the number is not limited.

![Hiding tabs that do not fit](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/03_How_to_use.png)

### Unavailable content

Do not remove or disable a tab when its functions are unavailable. Explain why a tab’s content is unavailable in the body of the tab.

## Placement

### Position

Always place tabs on top of the content. It is possible to place them at other sides — bottom, left, or right — but such a placement is extremely rare and might confuse users.

### Independent content

Do not place independent content under the tabs. Create separate tabs for such content.

Correct

![Correct placment of independent content](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/06_Placement_correct.png)
Incorrect

![Incorrect placement of independent content](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/06_Placement_incorrect.png)

### Controls above tabs

When there are other UI controls above tabs, separate them with a vertical indent.

![UI controls above the tabs](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/07_Placement_correct.png)

### Tabs border

* Make sure the border of the tab reaches the edges of the area tabs occupy.

* Do not surround the tab content area with a visible border.

Correct

![Correct bottom border](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/04_Placement_correct.png)
Incorrect

![Incorrect bottom border](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/04_Placement_incorrect.png)
Incorrect

![Frame around the tab content](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/05_Placement_incorrect.png)



# Text Area

<tldr>
Implementation: [JBTextArea](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/components/JBTextArea.java)
</tldr>

A text area allows users to enter or edit multi-line text.

![Text area example](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/text_area_example.png)

## When to use

Use a text area if input is unconstrained and long, or if the newline character is a valid value. Example: commit message or code snippets.

Do not use a text area if:

* Input consists of several words. Use an [input field](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/input-field.html) instead.

* There is not enough space for a text area, or if input is normally short but can occasionally be long or multi-line. Use an [expandable input field](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/input-field.html#when-not-to-use) instead.

* Values are added one by one. Use a [table](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/table.html) instead.

* Text is read-only. Use a [description text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/description-text.html) instead.

## How to use

### Label

Follow the rules for the [input field](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/input-field.html).

A label is required for all empty text areas.
If a text area is prefilled, and it’s clear from the context what data it contains, a label can be omitted.
For example, the following text area is used to preview file and code templates:

![No label](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/no_label.png)
If a new file template is added and the text area is empty, the label is required.

Do not put units on the right of the text area.

Do not use a [group header](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/group-header.html) instead of the text area label. The horizontal
line is redundant here. Use [context help](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/context-help.html) to explain the field behavior.

Incorrect

![Label incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/label_incorrect.png)
Correct

![Label correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/label_correct.png)

### Placeholder, prefilled values and field focus

Follow the rules for the input field: [placeholder](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/input-field.html#placeholder), [prefilled value](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/input-field.html#prefilled-value), [field focus](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/input-field.html#field-focus).

### History

If the previous user input should be saved, use `⌥↑` and `⌥↓` on macOS and `Alt+Up/Down`
on Windows and Linux to navigate through the history.
If history is available, add a note at the bottom of the input field:

![Text area history](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/text_area_history.png)
Save the current value, so that the user can return to it while navigating through the history.

### Validation

If the user types an invalid value, highlight the text area with red and show an error message in a tooltip. For more details, see [Validation errors](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/validation-errors.html).

![Text area error](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/text_area_error.png)

## Size and placement

Recommended sizes:

![Text area sizes](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/text_area_sizes.png)
This is the default size, it can be changed if the dialog is resized.

Height. The minimum text area height is 3 lines ~55px, so the user understands that it’s multi-line. The maximum height is not limited and should be appropriate for the most common values.

Width. The minimum text area width is 270px. It’s inconvenient to use a narrower field due to frequent line breaks. The maximum width is 80 symbols ~600px, otherwise, it’s hard to read the text.

Size the text area to display an integral number of lines of text:

| Incorrect |Correct |
----------------------
| ![Text area size 2](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/text_area_size_2.png) |![Text area size 3](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/text_area_size_3.png) |

Do not resize a text area on input. It will change the position of other controls and they can become hardly discoverable.

If the text is long and does not fit the text area, add [scrollbar](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/scrollbar.html).

For placement, follow the rules for the [input field](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/input-field.html).

## Style

Use the same colors as for the [input field](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/input-field.html).

Do not highlight a text area on selection, only if a validation error occurs.

### History

Background: dialog default theme color

Font: Windows, IntelliJ — default, macOS 2px smaller than default



# Toggle Button

<tldr>
Implementation: see [Control](#control)
</tldr>

The toggle button is used to switch between On and Off states.

![Toggle button example](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toggle_button_example.png)

## When to use

Use the toggle button to switch the state of an item in search results:

![Example se](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/example_se.png)
Do not use the toggle button for items in dialogs and menus. Instead, use a checkbox in dialogs and a checkmark in menus:

![When to use dialog or menu](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/when_to_use_dialog_or_menu.png)

## How to use

### Label

The toggle button in search results should duplicate the option from the settings or the menu.
Label and capitalization should be the same as on the option label:

![Label checkbox](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/label_checkbox.png)
Setting in the preferences

![Label checkbox se](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/label_checkbox_se.png)
The same setting in search results

Do not make a setting available only from search results.

If the setting is in a tree or menu, use the toggle button label to specify where the setting is located:

![Label tree](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/label_tree.png)
Setting in a tree

![Label tree se](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/label_tree_se.png)
The same setting in search results; separate tree levels with a colon

![Label menu](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/label_menu.png)
Setting in the main menu

![Label menu se](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/label_menu_se.png)
The same setting in search results; separate the first menu level with a vertical bar, and separate others with a colon

Refer to [checkbox](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/checkbox.html) for writing checkbox labels and menu labels.

Do not add the word "On" or "Off" to the item name, since the state description is already in the toggle button.

### Control

A toggle button is implemented with the [OnOffButton](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ui/components/OnOffButton.java) class.
But generally, you shouldn't use the class directly.
The IDE automatically places the buttons in the search feed if you follow one of the patterns described below:

1. If this is a system or editor or another kind of settings, register the corresponding [BooleanOptionDescription](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ide/ui/search/BooleanOptionDescription.java) for the option. The options can be bound (but not limited) to a [SearchTopHitProvider](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/ide/SearchTopHitProvider.kt) instance which is registered in `plugin.xml` with the `<search.topHitProvider implementation="fq.class.name"/>` tag.

For example, see the [SystemOptionsTopHitProvider](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-impl/src/com/intellij/ide/ui/SystemOptionsTopHitProvider.java) class that represents matching of Reopen last project on startup checkbox to `BooleanOptionDescription`.

2. Implement your own action that's inherited from [ToggleAction](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/openapi/actionSystem/ToggleAction.java) and registered in `plugin.xml`.

The toggle button changes state when it is clicked with the mouse or when `Enter` is pressed on the item line.



# Toolbar

<tldr>
Related: [Building a Toolbar/Popup Menu from Actions](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/action-system.html#buildingToolbarPopupMenu)
</tldr>

A toolbar provides quick access to frequently used actions and settings. It appears in dialogs, popups, tool windows, lists, trees, and tables.

![A toolbar with 6 icons and a drop-down list](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar.png)

## Toolbar items

![A toolbar with all kinds of UI controls that can appear on it: an action icon button, a drop-down icon button, a toggle icon button, a split icon button, a search field, a button, a label, a toolbar drop-down list and an overflow chevron](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_items.png)
The following controls can appear on a toolbar:

* [Icon button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/icon-button.html): action, toggle, or drop-down

* [Split icon button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/split-icon-button.html)

* [Toolbar drop-down list](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/toolbar-drop-down.html)

* [Search field](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/search-field.html)

* [Button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/button.html)

* Separator

* Label

* Chevron

## What items to add on toolbar

### Frequently used items

Add actions and settings that are frequently used:

* If usage statistics are available, frequent use is more than 5% of this feature's users.

* If usage statistics are not available: * Add items that are needed for the most common use cases of this feature. * If possible, add usage statistics logging for toolbar items that lack it. Check statistics after 3–4 weeks of use. If the items are used by less than 5% of the feature's users, consider removing them from the toolbar.

Note:
Exception: some actions can be used most frequently because they are widely known, like the Copy and Paste actions. Place such actions on the toolbar only if you want to promote them. Otherwise, place them only in a context menu or the main menu.

### New items

When adding a new action or setting for a UI area that already has a toolbar: if the new item is expected to be used frequently, add it to increase its discoverability.

## How to use

### Location

Toolbars can be horizontal or vertical. Which type to use, depends on what control the toolbar is used for.

#### Lists, trees, tables

Use horizontal toolbars for lists, trees, and tables that appear in dialogs and popups. Place the toolbar at the top of the control.

![A horizontal toolbar with 5 icons above a tree](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_dialogs_horizontal.png)

#### Vertical tool windows

Use horizontal toolbars in tool windows that are vertical by default.

![The Commit tool window with a horizontal toolbar above a tree with changes](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_vertical_tool_window.png)

#### Horizontal tool windows

Use vertical toolbars for tool windows that are horizontal by default. Place the toolbar on the left in a tool window.

![The Problems tool window with a vertical toolbar on the left of the tree with file errors](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_horizontal_tool_window.png)

If a horizontal tool window has several sections, place a toolbar on the right in sections after the first one if these conditions are true:

* The sections are a master-detail layout, with a list or tree on the left and a selected item's details on the right.

* The toolbar contains actions that are used occasionally, like the Soft-Wrap setting in the Console section of the Build tool window.

This way the toolbar would not break the connection between the master and the detail sections.

![The Build tool window with the vertical toolbar on the right of the Console section](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_horizontal_tool_window_at_right.png)

A horizontal toolbar can be used in a horizontal tool window in the two cases:

* The toolbar contains items used for managing processes, like Step In and Step Out in the Debug tool window, or Run and Stop in the Run tool window. A horizontal toolbar makes the actions more noticeable and easy to reach.

* The toolbar contains items that need horizontal space, like a search field and drop-down lists in the Git tool window.

![The Debug tool window with a horizontal toolbar containing the Run, Stop, Resume, Pause, Step In, Step Out and other actions](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_horizontal_tool_window_hor_toolbar_debug.png)![The Git tool window with a horizontal toolbar containing a search field and four drop-down lists with filters for the list of commits](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_horizontal_tool_window_hor_toolbar_git.png)

### Items alignment

On a vertical toolbar, always top-align items.

On a horizontal toolbar:

* Left-align items by default.

* Right-align the less frequently used items.

![The Keymap settings with a tree and a toolbar above it: the Expand, Collapse and Edit icon buttons are on the left side of the toolbar, and a search field with another icon button are on the right side](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_items_alignment.png)

### Items grouping

Group related toolbar items and separate groups with lines.

![A toolbar with three icon groups: Build, Run, Debug and Profile are the Run actions group; Git Update, Push, Diff and two more are the Git actions group; the Project Structure and Settings are the Settings group](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_items_grouping.png)

If there are several unrelated icons, do not add separators after each icon. Separators could be entirely omitted if there are 5 and fewer icons on a toolbar.

|              Correct             ![A toolbar with five icons without separators](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_separators_correct.png)          |Incorrect             ![A toolbar with five icons and three separators](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_separators_incorrect.png) |

#### Label

Label a group of icons if it helps to make the icons clearer and if it’s needed to promote the icons. The icons group becomes more visible with the label.

![A horizontal toolbar with three icon groups, with a label for one of the groups](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_items_grouping_with_label.png)

### Items order

Arrange separate items or groups in the following order by default.

If usage statistics are available, and popular items appear not at the top or left of a toolbar, consider arranging by the frequency of use.

![A vertical toolbar with icon categories ordered from top to bottom: actions, view options, an action to open a preview panel in a tool window, settings](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_items_order.png)

### Toolbar overflow

A toolbar's width is usually limited by the element it belongs to. If there is not enough space for items on the toolbar, they are hidden under a chevron. Hovering the chevron shows the hidden items.

It is recommended to keep the number of toolbar items to what would be visible by default. Otherwise, the items will be hidden and it will be hard to discover them.

|              ![A horizontal toolbar above a tree with seven icons and an overflow chevron at the right](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_overflow.png)          |             ![The same UI as in the previous image but with the overflow chevron hovered: the full toolbar with nine icons becomes visible](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_overflow_hover.png)          |

#### Avoid two toolbars

Do not counter a toolbar overflow by adding more toolbars. If there are too many items on a toolbar:

* Group items under drop-down icon buttons

* Remove unpopular items by following the guidelines in [What items to add on toolbar](#what-items-to-add-on-toolbar)

|              Correct             ![A vertical toolbar with seven icons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/more_toolbars_correct.png)          |             Incorrect             ![Two vertical toolbars stacked together with 19 icons in total](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/more_toolbars_incorrect.png)          |

### Toolbar border

For scrollable content in tool windows, do not show a toolbar border if the content is at the top scroll position. Show the border once the content is scrolled under the toolbar.

|              ![A tree with a toolbar above it. The tree is at the top scroll position, the toolbar border is not visible.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_scroll_top.png)          |             ![A tree with a toolbar above it. The tree is scrolled under the toolbar, the toolbar border is visible.](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_scroll_under.png)          |

In places other than tool windows, it is fine to always show the border.

## Customization

Provide the ability to customize toolbars in the main window. To do this, add the toolbar to the list on the `Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Menus and Toolbars` page.



# Icon Button

<tldr>
Implementation: [ActionButton](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-impl/src/com/intellij/openapi/actionSystem/impl/ActionButton.java)
</tldr>

| ![Using links instead of buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_icon_button.png) |             A toolbar icon button contains only an icon. There are three types of icon buttons:               * An action triggers immediately.    * A toggle switches between on and off states.    * A drop-down opens a menu.            |

## When to use

Follow the guidelines for the [Toolbar](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/toolbar.html#what-items-to-add-on-toolbar).

## How to use

### Icon

Use an [existing icon](https://intellij-icons.jetbrains.design) or create a new one following the [icon guidelines](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/icons-style.html).

### Tooltip

| ![Using links instead of buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_icon_button_tooltip.png) |Always provide a tooltip for an icon button. Include a shortcut if there is one. See [Tooltip](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/tooltip.html) for details. |

### States

| ![Using links instead of buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_icon_button_states.png) |When an action is not available in a particular context, disable the icon button. |

### Filter badge

![Using links instead of buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_icon_button_badge.png)
For filter actions, show a badge over an icon when a non-default option is selected. The badge helps to see if the content is in its default state or filtered.

### Search option icon

![Using links instead of buttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_icon_button_search_option.png)
Search option icons have a more noticeable pressed state to allow quickly seeing what affects the search results. See [Search options](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/search-field.html#search-options) for details.



# Split Icon Button

<tldr>
Implementation: [SplitButtonAction](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-impl/src/com/intellij/openapi/actionSystem/SplitButtonAction.java)
</tldr>

A split icon button appears on a horizontal [toolbar](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/toolbar.html) and consists of two parts: the main icon and a triangle icon for the action list.

![Split icon button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/split_icon_button.png)

## When to use

Use the split icon button to reduce the number of actions on a horizontal toolbar if all the following conditions are met:

* There are already many controls on the toolbar.

* There is a group of similar actions.

* The user invokes one action more often than others. Or the user invokes one action several times, then switches to another action and invokes it several times but does not switch between actions too often.

Note:
To decide whether to add actions to the toolbar, follow the [Toolbar](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/toolbar.html#what-items-to-add-on-toolbar) guidelines.

## How to use

### Add icons to all menu actions

Make sure that all actions in the drop-down menu have icons. When an action is selected, its icon will be shown on the toolbar.

![Split icon button main action icon](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/split_icon_button_main_action_icon.png)

### Disable unavailable actions

Do not hide the unavailable actions but show them as disabled to help users locate them in the future. The action menu should always open even if all the items in it are disabled.

![Split icon button disabled item](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/split_icon_button_disabled_item.png)



# Toolbar Drop-Down List

<tldr>
Implementation: [ComboBoxButton](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-api/src/com/intellij/openapi/actionSystem/ex/ComboBoxAction.java)
</tldr>

A toolbar drop-down list is a type of button that appears on a horizontal toolbar and shows a list of choices on clicking it.

![Toolbar dropdown example](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_dropdown_example.png)

## When to use

Use toolbar drop-down if a single option should be selected.

If the choices are objects or states.

To select values that are controlled by the toolbar button on the right.

![Toolbar main](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_main.png)
To filter values or change the appearance in the control below:

![Toolbar filter](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_filter.png)
Use a [toolbar drop-down button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/icon-button.html) instead of a drop-down list in the following cases:

* If there is a list of actions:

![Toolbar dropdown menu button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_dropdown_menu_button.png)
* The options are secondary and the user won’t change them in most cases.

* Multi-selection is required, for example, to group by several attributes.

Do not use toolbar drop-down in dialogs, use the [drop-down list](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/drop-down.html) instead.

| Incorrect |Correct |
----------------------
| ![Settings incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/settings_incorrect.png) |![Settings correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/settings_correct.png) |

## How to use

Do not add a label to the toolbar drop-down.

For the default value, follow the rules for the [drop-down list](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/drop-down.html#default-value).

Add separators between the toolbar drop-down and icons:

![Diff](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/diff.png)
If a drop-down is controlled by buttons, add a border, as separators will break the connection between the controlling icons and the drop-down:

![Toolbar main](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_main.png)
The toolbar drop-down does not get the focus. Highlight it on hover the same way as toolbar icons.

![Toolbar dropdown hover](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_dropdown_hover.png)
### Menu

#### Control

Open the drop-down menu when clicking anywhere on a drop-down list.
Open the menu down by default. If there is not enough space, open the menu up.

Select the first option when the menu opens.

Move the selection in the menu on pressing the Up and Down arrows or on hovering the cursor over the item.

Filter items in the list on typing:

![Search](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/search.png)
Close the menu if the user selects an item, clicks outside the menu, presses the Esc key or switches to another app.

Allow single-click activation using mouse: click on a drop-down, the drop-down opens, select an item by hovering,
close the drop-down with the new item selected by releasing the mouse button.

#### Menu items

Follow the rules for the [drop-down list](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/drop-down.html#menu-items).

If it’s necessary to configure options in a toolbar drop-down list, add customization actions at the top or at the bottom of the list
and separate them with a line.
Use title case capitalization for actions.

![Toolbar dropdown customize](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_dropdown_customize.png)
A toolbar drop-down list can have submenus.

### Submenu

A submenu is a menu item that shows a list of nested items. A submenu includes a triangular indicator that distinguishes it from other menu items.

Use item submenus to group related options and to show hierarchy:

![Submenu example](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/submenu_example.png)
Show the submenu list on hovering over an item.

If the selection moves with the Up and Down arrow keys, show the submenu list on pressing the Right arrow or the Enter key.

Avoid submenus inside submenus. Submenus hide choices too deep and are difficult to navigate.

## Sizes and placement

Toolbar drop-down sizes are the same for all themes.

![Toolbar dropdown sizes](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_dropdown_sizes.png)
The width changes depending on the selected value to save space if the value is short.

![Toolbar dropdown width](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolbar_dropdown_width.png)
For menu sizes see [Drop-down menu](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/drop-down.html#menu-items).



# Tool Window

A tool window is a pane inside the main IDE window. For information about tool windows, see [IntelliJ IDEA Web Help](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/tool-windows.html). For information about implementing tool windows, see [Tool Windows](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/tool-windows.html).

![Toolwindow](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolwindow.png)

## When to use

Tool windows provide access to information, tools, and services that support coding. They let users manage the project, run and debug applications, view git changes, and work with external systems — all without leaving the main workspace.

## Tool window structure

![Toolwindow structure](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolwindow_structure.png)
### Tool window name

* The name should be [short and descriptive](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/writing-short.html), preferably not longer than two words.

* Use title-case capitalization.

* Provide an abbreviation if a common one exists when tool window names are shown in the stripes. For example, `Pull Requests` becomes `PR`.

| ![Toolwindow name](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolwindow_name.png) |![Toolwindow name stripes](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolwindow_name_stripes.png) |

### Icon

Add an icon for the tool window button. The icon should be created in two sizes: 20×20px and 16×16px, grey, and monochromatic. See how to create icons in the [icons guidelines](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/icons-style.html).

#### Icon badge for feedback

Show a colored badge above the icon if the tool window content changes and can contain different types of feedback, for example, new updates or errors.

Do not change the icon for the tool window button when the content changes.

![Toolwindow badge](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolwindow_badge.png)

### Tabs

Add [tabs](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/tabs.html) to group related content or create similar instances, like run sessions, history for files, find results. The tabs for similar entities should be closable.

![Toolwindow tabs](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolwindow_tabs.png)

### Toolbar

Add a toolbar for [frequently used actions and filters](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/toolbar.html#what-items-to-add-on-toolbar). For more details, see the [toolbar guidelines](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/toolbar.html).

## How to use

### Visibility

If a tool window has no content yet, show its button by default only if the window contains basic functionality that is likely to be used for all projects, for example, Version Control or Problems. Otherwise, hide the tool window button by default. Hidden tool windows are still available under More tool windows menu.

| Correct![Toolwindow more correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolwindow_more_correct.png) |Incorrect![Toolwindow more incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolwindow_more_incorrect.png) |

Don't show the tool window button if the tool window is not relevant to the current project configuration. For example, don't show the Maven tool window for a project without Maven configuration files.

### Orientation

#### Vertical window

Vertical tool windows work better for trees, for example, Project, Structure, or Maven tool windows.

![Toolwindow vertical](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolwindow_vertical.png)

#### Horizontal window

Horizontal tool windows work better for tables, wide content, or master-detail panels, for example, Git Log, Terminal, or Problems.

![Toolwindow horizontal](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolwindow_horizontal.png)

### Empty state

If a tool window has no content yet, show [empty state](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/empty-state.html) to help users start working with the tool window.

| Correct![Toolwindow empty state correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolwindow_empty_state_correct.png) |Incorrect![Toolwindow empty state incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/toolwindow_empty_state_incorrect.png) |

Related: [Text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/ui-faq.html#text)

## Numbers

Note:

If there is a space between the number and the unit, use a non-breaking space.

|  | Examples  | When and how to use  |
---------------------------------------
| Numbers |4,255,165.00 |Space is not limited, e.g. Settings dialog:           ![Numbers](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/numbers.png)      |
| Numbers short |         10.5k           3.3M        |Space is limited, e.g. in table or lists. |
| Percentage |13% | |
| Ratios |3 of 10 | |
| Ratios short |3/10 |Space is limited, e.g. in table or lists. |
| Currency |$10 | |

## Date and time

By default, the date and time formats are taken from the system settings. The format can be changed on the `Settings | Appearance & Behavior | System Settings | Date Formats` page.

See the table below to understand in which cases to show date and time.

|  | Examples  | When and how to use  |
---------------------------------------
| Date |         Today           05 Jan           05 Jan 2017        |         Omit the time for events if the exact time does not matter, e.g., Annotate panel.           Use Today and Yesterday for the last two days, use exact date for all other days.           Do not show the year if it’s within the current calendar year.        |
| Date and time |         Today, 14:04           05 Jan, 14:04           05 Jan 2019, 14:04        |When it is important to know the exact sequence of actions, e.g., Version Control Log. |
| Time |22:49 |Omit date if the event happened today and it’s clear from the context. |
| Date and day of week |Tuesday, 30 August |         Use as headers in timelines, e.g., Event Log. The day of the week helps to quickly understand how long ago was the event.           Use Today and Yesterday for the last two days, use exact date for all other days.        |
| Approximate time |        A moment ago          10 minutes ago          2 hours ago        |Use for a single event that happened recently, e.g., in the Status bar:           ![Approximate](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/approximate.png)         Do not use in tables as it’s harder to compare.           If more than 12 hours have passed since the event, use Date format.        |

![Vcs log](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/vcs_log.png)
Version Control Log (in IntelliJ IDEA incorrect format is used at the moment)

![Event log](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/event_log.png)
Event Log

## Duration

|  | Examples  | When and how to use  |
---------------------------------------
| Period |         10 milliseconds           10 seconds           10 minutes           1 hour        |Space is not limited, e.g. Settings dialog:         ![Period](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/period.png)      |
| Time-lapse |         1 h 30 m 30 s           1 h 30 m 30.035 s           1 h           1 h 0 m 30 s           1 m 30 s           05 Jan 2019, 14:04        |Use for changing duration. Select units depending on the process type. E.g., Unit tests usually run less than a minute, so show only seconds and milliseconds. Build tasks usually run more than a minute, so show minutes and seconds.           Omit hours and seconds that do not provide additional data.    |
| Time-lapse condensed [ISO 8601 standard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) |1:30:01.350 |Use when space is limited or to describe a range, e.g. 1:30:01.350 – 1:30:02.350  |

Use decimal numeral system.

| bits |10 bits |
