## Units

All numeric values should be given a unit or clearly labeled if they do not have suitable units, e.g. counters.

![Period](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/period.png)![No units](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/no_units.png)
Select the most convenient units.

| Incorrect |Correct |
----------------------
| ![Connection incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/connection_incorrect.png) |![Connection correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/connection_correct.png) |

Place units after the input field.

| Incorrect |Correct |
----------------------
| ![Caret incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/caret_incorrect.png) |![Caret correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/caret_correct.png) |

## Tables

Use the rules below to make it easier to compare numbers in one column.

Right-align numeric values.

![Data formats table](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/data_formats_table.png)
Include the unit in the column header if all values share the same unit. Convert each number to use the same unit.
If it’s not possible, e.g., the scatter of numbers is too large, include the unit with each value.

| Incorrect |Correct |
----------------------
| ![Table units incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/table_units_incorrect.png) |![Table units correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/table_units_correct.png) |

Be consistent with the precision of the significand.

| Incorrect |Correct |
----------------------
| ![Precision incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/precision_incorrect.png) |![Precision correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/precision_correct.png) |



# Icons

Follow these guidelines to create a new icon or redesign an existing one for IntelliJ-based products.

Note:

See all icons in the [Icons list](https://intellij-icons.jetbrains.design).
Use the [IntelliJ Icons Figma plugin](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/ui-kit.html)
to quickly find and use icons in UI mockups.

## Style

A common style unites several icons into a set and makes them recognizable.

Use a flat geometric icon style with straight corners and edges. Flat icons remain legible even in small sizes.

Use flat shapes instead of complex 3D forms:

| Incorrect |Correct |
----------------------
| ![Style pin 3d](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/style_pin_3d.png) |![Style pin flat](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/style_pin_flat.png) |

Use straight corners and lines instead of curves. It’s recommended to use 45° and 90° angles, or 30° and 60° where possible:

| Incorrect |Correct |
----------------------
| ![Style folder round](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/style_folder_round.png) |![Style folder straigt](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/style_folder_straigt.png) |

Icons should be as simple as possible without losing their meaning. Clean and simple icons ensure readability and reduce visual clutter.

|  Incorrect  | Correct  |
--------------------------
|  ![Style soft wrap detailed](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/style_soft_wrap_detailed.png)  | ![Style soft wrap simple](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/style_soft_wrap_simple.png)  |
| Reduced the icon to its minimal form, without losing its meaning. |

## Grid and size

Basically, icons fit into a square artboard. Leave a transparent padding around the perimeter. For default 16px icons, the transparent border is 1px, so the icon’s visible part should be inside the 14px x 14px area.

![Grid](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/grid.png)
14px x 14px is the area where the visible part of the icon should fit for a 16px icon.

Content should only go beyond the borders if a [modifier](#modifier) is added, or if additional visual weight is required.

Sizes for other icon sizes can be found in the table below:

|  Icon Type  | Icons Size  | Transparent Border  |
---------------------------------------------------
|  Gutter, status bar  | 12px x 12px  | —  |
|  Tool window  | 13px x 13px  | —  |
|  Default: toolbar icons, project tree, etc.  | 16px x 16px  | 1px, except for modifier  |
|  Dialogs  | 32px x 32px  | 2px  |
|  Logo app icon  |          32px x 32px            64px x 64px            128px x 128px            256px x 256px            512px x 512px        | —  |

## Basic shapes

Use basic shapes to build icons, such as squares, circles and rectangles. Using a grid and basic shapes ensures consistent visual proportions and placement.

| ![Shape square](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/shape_square.png) Square 12px x 12px |![Shape circle](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/shape_circle.png) Circle 14px |
| ![Shape rect horizontal](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/shape_rect_horizontal.png) Horizontal rectangle 10px x 14px |![Shape rect vertical](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/shape_rect_vertical.png) Vertical rectangle 14px x 10px |

Make sure that icons have the same visual weight. The more filled an icon is, the less space it needs. Following this rule, circles, rhombuses, triangles and other non-square shapes should have larger height and width to be optically balanced with square figures.

![Shapes weight 1](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/shapes_weight_1.png)
Make the circle diameter 2px bigger than square icons’ height to compensate for the visual weight.

Icons with more details should occupy more space.

![Shapes weight 2](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/shapes_weight_2.png)
The eye icon is less detailed and occupies less space than a more complex scissors icon.

Icon weight can often take priority over the basic shape sizing. For more examples on visual weight compensation, see [Optical Effects in User Interfaces](https://medium.muz.li/optical-effects-9fca82b4cd9a).

## Stroke

Use a 2px stroke as the main drawing line. Consistent line weight makes icons cohesive.

|  ![Stroke download](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/stroke_download.png) | ![Stroke calc](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/stroke_calc.png) |
| Use consistent stroke width. |A thinner stroke can be used for subtle tweaks to the legibility of an icon and for optical correction. |

Align pixels on the X and Y axis and round to the nearest whole pixel, or 0.5px if it’s not possible to align to integer pixels. Aligning icons off the pixel grid will make the icon blurry when it’s rasterized.

Note:

To check what an icon will look like when rasterized use the `View | Canvas | Show Pixels on Zoom` option `Ctrl+P` in Sketch,
`View | Pixel Preview` `Alt+Ctrl+Y` in Illustrator.

| Incorrect |Correct |
----------------------
| ![Stroke pixels incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/stroke_pixels_incorrect.png)           If an icon is positioned off pixels,   it becomes blurry when rasterized.  |![Stroke pixels correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/stroke_pixels_correct.png)           Position stokes on integer pixels where possible.  |

Use the 30°, 45° and 60° angles for diagonal lines as they look sharper than diagonals with other angles.

Round shapes, small details and some letters cannot be aligned to the pixel grid. Make sure that the significant pixels have sufficient saturation.

Reduce the number of anchors as they increase the size of the image and takes longer to process it.

| Incorrect |Correct |
----------------------
| ![Stroke anchors incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/stroke_anchors_incorrect.png)           Unneeded anchors are added.  |![Stroke anchors correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/stroke_anchors_correct.png)           Use the minimum number of anchors.  |

## Modifier

A modifier is a small shape added over the base icon.

The default modifier position is the bottom right corner. If the base shape is badly recognizable with a modifier in the bottom right corner, or if several modifiers are needed, the modifier can be placed in other corners.

|  ![Modifier search](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/modifier_search.png)             Place the modifier in the left corner   if the base shape is badly recognizable   with the modifier in the right corner.  | ![Modifier parameter](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/modifier_parameter.png)             Place the modifier in the left corner   if there are several modifiers.  |

A modifier size is from 6px to 9px, depending on the shape's weight.
Leave a 1-2px spacing between the modifier and the main shape, to make the modifier clearly visible.

![Modifier size](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/modifier_size.png)
Modifier sizes

## Arrows

General rules for arrows: arrowhead is a filled triangle with a 90° pointing angle, a 2px body ends in a square stroke. An arrow’s orientation is horizontal, vertical, 45° or round.

![Arrows basic](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/arrows_basic.png)
Basic arrow icons

Unfilled arrowhead can be used if there is only one arrow on an icon to reduce excessive visual weight, for example, for navigation arrows, such as back and forward, up and down.

|  ![Arrow filled](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/arrow_filled.png) | ![Arrow unfilled](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/arrow_unfilled.png) |
|  90° arrowhead and 2px square stroke body. | Back arrow with unfilled arrowhead to compensate visual weight. |

Do not use other arrow styles, for example, unfilled arrows or arrows with thinned tails.

Incorrect

![Arrows incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/arrows_incorrect.png)

## Color

Do not use color as the only differentiator between icons (except for the [Noun icon](#noun-icons)) because some people do not distinguish colors. Make sure that icons are easily distinguishable by their shape.

Do not use gradients or shadows.

### Action icons

An action icon is an icon that triggers an action. It usually appears on toolbars and in dialogs.
There are 5 colors in the action icons palette.
The dark version is for Darcula theme.

|              ![Action red](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/action_red.png)                           Red  #DB5860            |             ![Action red d](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/action_red_d.png)                           Red dark  #C75450            |
|              ![Action yellow](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/action_yellow.png)                           Yellow  #EDA200            |             ![Action yellow d](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/action_yellow_d.png)                           Yellow dark  #F0A732            |
|              ![Action green](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/action_green.png)                           Green  #59A869            |             ![Action green d](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/action_green_d.png)                           Green dark  #499C54            |
|              ![Action blue](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/action_blue.png)                           Blue  #389FD6            |             ![Action blue d](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/action_blue_d.png)                           Blue dark  #3592C4            |
|              ![Action grey](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/action_grey.png)                           Grey  #6E6E6E            |             ![Action grey d](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/action_grey_d.png)                           Grey dark  #AFB1B3            |

Use these colors according to the following rules:

1. By default, action icons are grey and monochromatic:

![Colors actions grey](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/colors_actions_grey.png)

2. If an icon falls into one of the categories below, use the corresponding color:

|  Green Positive actions: run, create   ![Colors actions green](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/colors_actions_green.png)  | Red Destructive actions: stop, remove, force   ![Colors actions red](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/colors_actions_red.png)  |
|  Blue Accent color to highlight popular icons based on usage statistics, highlight small elements in complex icons    ![Colors actions blue](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/colors_actions_blue.png)  | Yellow Warning actions: attract attention to the places (e.g., code) that can be optimized or improved    ![Colors actions yellow](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/colors_actions_yellow.png)  |

3. Preserve colors in icon combinations. If an icon is colored in its full size, it should have the same color when reduced.

![Colors actions modifier](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/colors_actions_modifier.png)

4. Use green and red colors for paired icons. Color helps distinguish between similar icons faster.

![Colors actions pair](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/colors_actions_pair.png)

5. Use grey color for tool window icons. Icons are placed on the perimeter of the IDE, so they should not attract too much attention and distract users.

![Colors toolbuttons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/colors_toolbuttons.png)

### Status icons

Color is a great way to provide status information. Use status icons that are already present in the IDE repository:

![Colors status](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/colors_status.png)
If you need a new icon, color it according to its semantics. Make sure that the status icons are easily distinguishable by their form, as many colorblind people find it difficult to distinguish between red and green.

### Noun icons

A noun icon is an icon that appears in the tree view to mark different file types. It helps to locate items in the list faster and does not trigger an action.

The palette for noun icons is wider, because there are lots of icons in one set:

|              ![Noun grey](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/noun_grey.png)                           Grey  #9AA7B0            |             ![Noun grey 80](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/noun_grey_80.png)                           Grey 80%  #9AA7B0 op. 80%            |             ![Noun grey 60](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/noun_grey_60.png)                           Grey 60%  #9AA7B0 op. 60%            |

Select colors for new icons based on existing colors and users’ habits.

Use colors with 60% opacity and grey 80% for big parts, like folder icons:

![Colors nouns folder](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/colors_nouns_folder.png)
Transparent icons are used in both light and dark themes, so in most cases there’s only one version.

Use colors with 70% opacity for medium size elements that occupy about half of an icon, like file type icons:

![Colors nouns file](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/colors_nouns_file.png)
Use colors without opacity for small elements, like modifiers.

![Colors nouns modifier](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/colors_nouns_modifier.png)

## Font

To make a new icon with a letter, reuse letters from existing icons. If there's no suitable letter in existing icons, use a common sans-serif font like Arial or Open Sans.

## Export Icons

Note:

Install the [Svgo-compressor plugin](https://www.sketchapp.com/extensions/plugins/svgo-compressor/) in Sketch to optimize icons before save.

Use the SVG format for icons files. Use camelCase capitalization for icon names:

`iconName.svg`

If an icon is not the same in the dark theme, then also create:

`iconName_dark.svg`



# Layout

Arrange UI controls in dialogs according to the rules below to help people locate the necessary settings faster and understand how they are related.

Independent controls:

* [Labeled input controls](#labeled-input-controls): fields, combo boxes, text areas, etc.

* [Checkboxes and radio buttons](#checkboxes-and-radio-buttons)

* [Buttons and links](#buttons-and-links)

* [Lists, trees, tables](#lists-trees-and-tables)

[Dependent controls](#dependent-controls)— controls that depend on a parent control.

Organize controls into easily readable groups with [vertical and horizontal insets](#organize-with-insets).

## Independent controls

### Labeled input controls

Labeled input controls are: [input field](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/input-field.html), [combo box](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/combo-box.html), [drop-down list](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/drop-down.html), [text area](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/text-area.html), and spinner.

By default, put input controls with labels of similar length on different lines and align their input boxes on the left side.

![1 01 input similar labels](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/1_01_input_similar_labels.png)
Do not align input boxes on the left side if one label is twice as long as the other one or even longer.

![1 02 input different labels incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/1_02_input_different_labels_incorrect.png)![1 02 input different labels correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/1_02_input_different_labels_correct.png)
If several related input controls have labels of up to 10 characters and their input boxes are short, organize them in two columns. Do not use more than two columns.

![1 03 short inputs](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/1_03_short_inputs.png)
If an input box is long, and the horizontal space is limited, place the label above the box. Otherwise, always put the label and the box on the same line.

![1 04 input top label](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/1_04_input_top_label.png)
#### Separated by other controls

If there are two input controls with labels of similar length that are separated from each other by a single control, align their input boxes on the left side.

![1 05 separated by one](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/1_05_separated_by_one.png)
Align only the input boxes of the neighboring input controls. If there are several input controls on a page, and they are separated from each other by two or more other UI elements, do not align their input boxes.

![1 06 separated by two](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/1_06_separated_by_two.png)
If input groups are separated by a group of other UI controls, align only the boxes located within one group.

![1 07 separated groups](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/1_07_separated_groups.png)

#### Labels and right borders

Always left-align labels.

Note:

This alignment is inconsistent with macOS guidelines, but the aim is to maintain consistency in all JetBrains IDEs on all supported platforms.

![1 08 label alignment](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/1_08_label_alignment.png)
Align the right borders of input boxes that have a similar length. For alignment, use [built-in icons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/built-in-button.html). Do not use buttons.

![1 09 built in button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/1_09_built_in_button.png)

### Checkboxes and radio buttons

By default, put independent checkboxes and radio button groups on different lines.

![2 01 checkbox radio column](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/2_01_checkbox_radio_column.png)
If there is a group of 2–3 checkboxes with short labels (1–3 words), place them on the same line.
The same rule applies to radio buttons.
With this alignment, controls form a short sentence, making it easier to understand their meaning compared to when they are split into several lines.

![2 02 checkbox radio line](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/2_02_checkbox_radio_line.png)
When there is an input control on one line and a group of checkboxes or radio buttons on the next line, and their labels are of similar length
(one is no more than 5 characters longer than the other), align the input box with the checkbox/radio button.

If one label is much longer than the other, do not align these UI elements.

![2 03 align group labels](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/2_03_align_group_labels.png)
If a checkbox group does not have a label, align it with other independent controls by the left side.

![2 03 align without group labels](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/2_03_align_without_group_labels.png)
4 and more checkboxes can be arranged in columns:

* Arrange checkboxes with labels of up to 30 characters in 2 columns.

![2 04 checkbox 2 columns](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/2_04_checkbox_2_columns.png)
* Arrange checkboxes with labels of up to 15 characters in 3 columns.

![2 05 checkbox 3 columns](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/2_05_checkbox_3_columns.png)
Do not arrange radio buttons from one group in several columns. Splitting a group of radio buttons into two or more columns makes it unclear that all these radio buttons belong to the same setting.

![2 06 radio columns incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/2_06_radio_columns_incorrect.png)

### Buttons and links

Align an independent button or link to the left with other controls.

![3 01 button column](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/3_01_button_column.png)![3 01 link column](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/3_01_link_column.png)
If there are 2–3 buttons or links with labels of up to 30 characters each, place them on one line.

![3 02 button line](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/3_02_button_line.png)
Do not arrange buttons or links in several columns. Such a layout takes more time to parse visually.

![3 03 button columns](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/3_03_button_columns.png)

### Lists, trees and tables

Choose a control width such that most of the common values are visible. Take the whole width of the dialog if necessary.

![4 01 table full width](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/4_01_table_full_width.png)
If the dialog containing the control is noticeably wider than the control itself, reduce the length of the control.

Do not put other independent controls to the right of a list, tree, or table.
They would look like dependent controls in the master-detail layout.

![4 02 table fixed width](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/4_02_table_fixed_width.png)
If there are several lists, trees, or tables in a dialog, make them of the same width.

![4 03 aligned lists](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/4_03_aligned_lists.png)

## Dependent controls

Align controls according to the rules below to show that they are related.

Place 2–3 related UI controls on the same line if each control takes up to 30 characters. This way the user needs to read just one line, and it is quicker to see that the controls depend on each other.

![5 01 dependent one line](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/5_01_dependent_one_line.png)
In all other cases, place interrelated controls on different lines:

Main control: labeled input control.

* Align other dependent elements with the left border of the input box.

![5 03 dependent on field checkbox](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/5_03_dependent_on_field_checkbox.png)![5 03 dependent on field button](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/5_03_dependent_on_field_button.png)
* If an input's label is long or the input box is very short, align by the label and add a horizontal inset.

![5 04 dependent on field long label](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/5_04_dependent_on_field_long_label.png)
Main control: checkbox or radio button. Align dependent controls by the label.

![5 02 dependent on checkbox](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/5_02_dependent_on_checkbox.png)
When the main control or one of the dependent controls takes the whole width of a panel, left align all elements.

![5 05 whole width text area](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/5_05_whole_width_text_area.png)
The text area is the main control, the button is the dependent control.

![5 06 whole width checkbox](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/5_06_whole_width_checkbox.png)
The checkbox is the main control, the table is the dependent control.

When the main control takes the whole width of a panel, and there is one small dependent control (for example, a drop-down list), place this dependent control to the top-right corner, above the main control.

![5 07 whole width top right corner](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/5_07_whole_width_top_right_corner.png)
See the [Inline help text](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/inline-help-text.html#placement) and [Tooltip](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/tooltip.html#question-mark-icon-for-help-tooltips) articles for details on how to arrange help information in dialogs.

If controls do not depend on each other, left-align them all. Otherwise, the user might think that controls are linked.

![5 09 incorrect alignment](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/5_09_incorrect_alignment.png)
The spinners do not depend on the top checkbox.

## Organize with insets

Use vertical insets to break a list of controls into easily readable groups. Compare:

Incorrect

![6 02 group insets incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/6_02_group_insets_incorrect.png)
The list of controls is hard to scan quickly because the controls "stick" together.

Correct

![6 02 group insets correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/6_02_group_insets_correct.png)
Scanning a list of controls becomes easier when vertical insets are added between the groups of controls.

Treat insets with extra care and make sure that elements within a group are actually related. An unnecessary inset may create a false impression that the controls are grouped. This complicates the UI and might cause confusion.

Incorrect

![6 04 inset incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/6_04_inset_incorrect.png)
The first checkbox depends on the combo box which is shown with the horizontal inset. However, the checkboxes appear grouped because they are closer.

Correct

![6 04 inset correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/6_04_inset_correct.png)
The first checkbox is closer to its main control, and it is easier to see that the combo box and checkbox are related.

Horizontal insets also matter for grouping controls.

Incorrect

![6 05 hor inset incorrect](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/6_05_hor_inset_incorrect.png)
The checkboxes and the "Length" fields look independent because the horizontal inset between them is bigger than the vertical inset below the second checkbox.

Better

![6 05 hor inset better](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/6_05_hor_inset_better.png)
With smaller horizontal and bigger vertical insets, the checkboxes and the "Length" fields look related. However, it could be made better if the repeating word "Separator" appears only once.

Correct

![6 05 hor inset correct](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/6_05_hor_inset_correct.png)
Correct grouping and no duplicates help understand the UI quicker.

See [Groups of controls](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/groups-of-controls.html) for how to organize a bigger group of controls.



# Groups of Controls

Group controls to organize content on a screen and help people locate the necessary controls faster.

Use the following controls or layouts:

* [Group headers](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/group-header.html)

* [Tabs](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/tabs.html)

* Master-detail layout

## What grouping to choose

Use group headers if all rules apply:

Note:

If there are less than 3 controls in all groups, consider separating with [vertical insets](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/group-header.html#how-to-use).

* Each group contains no more than 10 controls

* All groups occupy no more than 2 heights of the dialog in its default size

![6 01 group headers](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/6_01_group_headers.png)
Use tabs if all rules apply:

* One of the groups contains more than 10 controls, or groups occupy more than 2 heights of a dialog

* There are no more than 8 groups

![01 use tabs](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/01_use_tabs.png)
Use the master-detail layout if either of the rules applies:

* There are more than 8 groups

* The number of groups can change

![02 use master detail](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/02_use_master_detail.png)



# Mnemonics

A mnemonic is an alphanumeric character, which indicates the key to press to activate a command or navigate to a component.

There are regular and numeric mnemonics.

* Regular mnemonics are used inside the text. The mnemonic is underlined in this case to be distinguishable. In a control: ![Inside](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/inside.png)In a menu: ![Menu](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/menu.png)Activate the control by pressing the mnemonic with: * Alt modifier key on Windows/Linux * Ctrl+Alt modifier keys on macOS.

* Numeric mnemonics are used as the first numeric character of an action in a popup: ![First](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/first.png) Invoke the action by pressing the corresponding number key.

## When to use

Specify mnemonics wherever possible in menus and controls. Mnemonics make the functionality more usable for power users who interact through the keyboard. Moreover, mnemonics make the functionality accessible for users with disabilities.

If there are many actions and/or controls, and it is not possible to assign mnemonics for all of them:

* Provide mnemonics for the most frequently used actions/controls.

* Provide mnemonics for [group headers](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/group-header.html) for quick navigation to the first element of the group.

Note: The rules for using numeric mnemonics in popups are under discussion. [Contact us](https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issues/IJSDK) if you have questions.

## How to use

![Letters](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/letters.png)
Make mnemonics in the label discoverable, they must be easy to find:

* Use letters at the beginning of the first or second word of the label.

* Use letters with wide widths, such as w, m, and capital letters.

* Avoid using letters that are difficult to see when they are assigned to underlined keys. These letters include: * Letters with descenders, such as g, j, p, q, or y. * Letters next to a letter with a descender. * Letters that are only one pixel wide, such as i or l.

Make it easy to remember for the most frequently used actions:

* Use standard Windows mnemonic if any. For example, Properties, Rename, Delete, Cut, Copy, Paste, Exit, etc. Note that Windows users are more likely to form habits for mnemonics as mnemonics are not that common on macOS or Linux.

* Do not use silent letters. For example, Design, Column, etc.

Do not assign mnemonics to the default or Cancel buttons. The default button is typically assigned to the ENTER key, and Cancel is assigned to the ESC key.

Do not use the same mnemonic letter twice in the same window; duplicated mnemonics confuse users. If you need to assign a new mnemonic in an existing context, check that it's not already taken. If it is, prioritize the mnemonic for the more frequently used action.



# Platform Theme Colors

There are two default color themes: IntelliJ Light and Darcula.

![01 default themes](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/01_default_themes.png)

Use the colors consistently within the default themes. To do so, follow these guidelines:

* [Icons](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/icons.html)

* UI components

* Editor scheme TBD

* Chart TBD

## UI components

Colors for UI components are specified with color keys.
A color key is a name of a color property in a particular component, e.g. `ComboBox.background`, or a generic color property for several components, e.g. `Component.borderColor`.

![02 keys naming](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/02_keys_naming.png)
Color keys of a combo box

Each key has two default color values: one for IntelliJ Light and another for Darcula. Example: `ComboBox.background` is #FFFFFF in IntelliJ Light and #3C3F41 in Darcula.

Keys allow creating [custom color themes](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/themes-getting-started.html). A custom theme is one of the default themes plus a set of color keys with new values in a JSON file. Example: the High contrast theme is a custom theme based on Darcula. New color values are stored in the [HighContrast.theme.json](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-resources/src/themes/HighContrast.theme.json) JSON file.

See custom themes in the [JetBrains Marketplace](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/search?tags=Theme) repository.

See the meanings of the parts in a color key in the [key naming scheme](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/themes-metadata.html#key-naming-scheme).

See a complete list of keys with their descriptions in the JSON files: [IntelliJPlatform.themeMetadata.json](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-resources/src/themes/metadata/IntelliJPlatform.themeMetadata.json), [JDK.themeMetadata.json](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-resources/src/themes/metadata/JDK.themeMetadata.json).

See the color values for the currently selected theme in the LaF Defaults dialog:

Tip:

To store color values between theme switching, use a scratch `*.theme.json` file.
This might be useful if you want to test colors before implementing them.
See guidelines for the [Theme JSON Structure](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/themes-customize.html#defining-named-colors).

* The dialog is available in the [internal mode](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/enabling-internal.html). See `Tools | Internal Actions | UI` in the main menu or find it with Help | Find Action.

* Some color keys are not shown in the dialog by default because they are loaded at runtime with a corresponding UI component. Open the UI with this component to see such keys in the dialog.

* Edit a color in the dialog to preview it in the IDE. The edited color is stored until the theme is switched.

![03 la f defaults](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/images/03_LaF_Defaults.png)
Note:

For IntelliJ designers:

* Provide color keys in design specifications to be sure that the correct keys are used.

* When a new key is implemented, check that [IntelliJPlatform.themeMetadata.json](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-resources/src/themes/metadata/IntelliJPlatform.themeMetadata.json) has the new key with the `since` parameter and description, and the old keys are deprecated.

If a color is needed:

1. Choose a color value for all default themes:

* Try reusing any of the existing colors first. Use the LaF Defaults dialog to see the existing colors.

* If none of them fit, choose two new color values that are consistent with IntelliJ Light and Darcula palettes in hue and contrast.

1. Choose a color key if a component does not have it:

* Use an existing color key if it fits semantically. Otherwise, a UI component might get an unexpected color in a custom color theme.

* Create a new key if none of the existing ones fit semantically. Follow the naming scheme.

Example

Incorrect: A new component with a light-blue background reuses `Focus.borderColor`, which has a light-blue color in the default themes. A theme author decides they need a bright focus border and changes the color value for `Focus.borderColor`. As a result, the new component has a bright background with the text unreadable over it.

Correct: A new component with a light-blue background has its own color key `ComponentName.background`.

Implementation
Use `JBColor.namedColor` to set a color key and fallback color values:

Kotlin:

```KOTLIN
val SELECTED_BACKGROUND_COLOR: Color =
    JBColor.namedColor(
        "CompletionPopup.selectionBackground",
        JBColor(0xc5dffc, 0x113a5c)
    )
```

Java:

```JAVA
private static final Color SELECTED_BACKGROUND_COLOR =
    JBColor.namedColor(
        "CompletionPopup.selectionBackground",
        new JBColor(0xc5dffc, 0x113a5c)
    );
```



# Typography

## UI font

[Inter](https://github.com/rsms/inter) is used for the IDE user interface by default. The default font size is the same for all supported OS: 13.

Users can change the default font in Settings | Appearance. If the default font size is changed, other font sizes used in the UI are scaled respectively.

Use the built-in text styles from the table below whenever possible.

Note:

Implementation example for font styles: [LabelSizeDemoAction](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/tree/idea/261.25134.95/platform/platform-impl/internal/src/com/intellij/internal/LabelSizeDemoAction.kt)

|  Font  | Font size  | Usage Examples  |
-----------------------------------------
|  H1 `JBFont.h1().asBold()`   | Default +5  |         Main page header. Example: Plugin name      |
|  H2 `JBFont.h2().asBold()`   | Default +3  |         Small page header. Example: Headers in a plugin description      |
|  Default `JBFont.regular()`   | Default  |         Main UI font. Examples: Labels, inputs, links, trees, tables, and other controls      |
|  Default semibold  `JBFont.regular().asBold()`    | Default  |         Header in dialogs, popups, notifications, tool windows, Got It tooltips        |
|  Paragraph  |          Default            Line height default +3        |         Multiline description text      |
| Medium `JBFont.medium()`   |Default –1 |         Help text      |
|  Medium semibold `JBFont.medium().asBold()`    |Default –1 |         Group headers in popups      |

If none of the built-in sizes work and a custom one is needed, define it as the default size +/- constant value. Do not hardcode font sizes.
